Nationwide plays the long game in women’s soccer
article_text:
Nationwide Insurance has scored a multi-year extension of its deal to be the official insurance sponsor of the National Women’s Soccer League.

Nationwide held on to its position as presenting sponsor of the Lauren Holiday Impact Award, which honors NWSL players for outstanding community service and character off the pitch.

Nationwide will kick in a $50,000 donation to a charitable organization of the winner’s choice once announced, which will air Thursday on ESPN2 at 6:30 p.m. Eastern time, the insurer said in a statement.

To date, Nationwide has already passed on more than $600,000 to nonprofits selected by clubs and players through the Nationwide Community Impact Award and the Lauren Holiday Impact Award.

Columbus, Ohio-based Nationwide has been a league partner since 2021.

Several NWSL athletes will also get a chance to trade their cleats for office shoes when Nationwide hosts its annual “Experience Nationwide” professional development event at its Columbus headquarters beginning Nov. 30. The event is aimed at helping players score career opportunities beyond the pitch.

title: UOB Confluence 2026 brings 11 South-east Asian artists to Singapore
article_text:
[SINGAPORE] Soil, lacquer, embroidery and oil paint are just some of the materials used in Confluence 2026, a Singapore exhibition offering a cross-section of contemporary South-east Asian art – and a chance for visitors to buy it.

Held at All About Art Gallery in Tanjong Pagar Distripark until Dec 6, the exhibition presents 23 works by 11 winners of the UOB Painting of the Year competition, Singapore’s longest-running art competition and one of South-east Asia’s most prestigious.

Now in its second year, Confluence has expanded beyond its Singapore-only debut to include artists from Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam. The artists differ widely in experience, background and technique, but several share an interest in how memory and identity are shaped by the places we inhabit.

In the Singapore contingent is Tang Kok Soo, who won both the Singapore and Southeast Asian Painting of the Year awards in October. The former semiconductor engineer, who turned to art full-time, contributes works that reflect his interest in geometry and meditative repetition.

Indonesian artist Mutiara Riswari takes a more material approach with her 180 cm by 140 cm Bentang Pulang that combines soil, resin, acrylic and charcoal, linking the land itself to ideas of belonging and the body.

From Vietnam, Tran Viet Long revisits the country’s lacquer-painting tradition in Landscape No 1 and Wave 1, while Thailand’s Tudpong Outayamagul uses Japanese mineral pigments and tempera for Spirit of the Forest.

Co-organised by UOB and All About Art Gallery, Confluence makes the artworks available for purchase, extending the competition’s support for artists beyond cash prizes and giving them another route towards finding collectors.

Confluence 2026 runs until Dec 6 at All About Art Gallery, 39 Keppel Road, #02-01E. Admission is free.

Fiji names seven debutants for opening SVNS rounds

The squads feature a blend of experienced campaigners and emerging talent, with debutants marked by an asterisk in the official team announcement.

In the Fijiana squad, captain Ana Naimasi will lead a side that includes Sesenieli Donu, Adi Salote Nailolo, Merewairita Neivosa, Laisani Mocesawana, Reapi Ulunisau, Varanisese Qoro, Kelerayani Luvu, Mariana Talatoka, Regan Chapman, Atelaite Ralivanawana, Ivi Savu and Mere Vocevoce.

The new caps in the women’s squad are Merewairita Neivosa and Regan Chapman.

For the men’s team, captain Tira Wilagi heads a squad featuring Akuila Dranivotua, Joseva Talacolo, Vilimone Raiqiso, Kavekini Tanivanuakula, George Bose, Aquino Savenaca, Douglas Daveta, Iowane Teba, Filipe Sauturaga, Sanaila Daliga, Vuiviwa Naduvalo and Saimone Qeleca.

The debutants in the men’s squad are Vilimone Raiqiso, Aquino Savenaca, Sanaila Daliga and Saimone Qeleca.

Both teams will begin their HSBC SVNS campaign in Dubai before travelling to Cape Town for the second tournament of the new season.

title: USA Names 1st Roster of HSBC SVNS Season
article_text:
The USA Women’s Eagles have named their roster for the opening leg of the 2026-2027 HSBC SVSN season in Dubai. The tournament kicks off Saturday, Nov. 28, and the Americans will do work in Pool A against Spain, Australia and France. All action will be broadcast live on Paramount+. [lead photo: Alex Ho @hoiho_photo]

“We’ve framed the whole cycle as building our house,” head coach Emilie Bydwell looked at the four years between Olympics. “2025 was about forming and foundation building, identifying our new group, and building depth while Paris Olympians took extended breaks or recovered. Last year was about framing our house; getting stability in our squad profile and game model for LA.

“This year is about storm-proofing that performance and building the squad,” the coach continued. “If we have injuries to experienced players, or teams start to figure out how we’re playing, we want to be able to adapt by deploying different roles and combinations. Our goal is to be a really adaptable and anti-fragile team through these first four tournaments and build squad capabilities regardless of the mix of experienced to less experienced players.”

A warm-up tournament in New Zealand punctuated the Eagles’ eight-week pre-season. Since returning home the team has focused on refining systems, testing players and combinations, and elevating standards.

“We’ve come back into these two weeks of training hitting the ground running,” head coach Emilie Bydwell said. “We still have stuff that we need to clean up and can still be better. Our preseason was a long eight weeks before we were in New Zealand, and no matter how well it’s planned, it’s just not the same as playing.”

Kristi Kirshe resumes the role of team captain and oversees a Dubai squad that includes Olympian Ilona Maher.

“Beyond who she is as a player, she’s such a professional,” Bydwell said. “She takes what she does here very seriously, and she’s such a competitor. It’s been really great to have her back in — ready to compete, ready to drive the standards that we have as a team, and ready to empower the young athletes that she’s playing alongside.”

On the opposite end of the experience spectrum, Utahan teenager Fane Tausinga is traveling to the UAE in hopes of earning a first USA 7s cap.

The Dubai SVNS kicks off on Saturday, Nov. 28, and USA will compete in Pool A start against Spain (1 a.m. EST), followed by fellow New Zealand invitational attendees Australia (4:22 a.m.) and France (8:46 a.m.). Knockouts follow on Sunday, and all of the action will livestream on Paramount+.

title: MLB’s Local Media Rights Emerge As Focus in Labor Fight
article_text:
The future of MLB’s local media business has become a central element in the sport’s labor battle, providing yet another substantial layer to the already fractious situation.

For the last six months, MLB club owners have proposed to pool the local media revenue of all 30 clubs as part of a sought-after economic system that would implement a hard salary cap and floor. Most recently, management has updated its cap offer to the MLB Players Association to a 2028 implementation, and vows there will be “no compromise” on the pursuit of a cap as the Dec. 1 expiration of the current labor deal and an expected lockout thereafter approach.

The pooling of local media revenues, and a promise to end regional blackouts that have long frustrated fans, were also part of a video recently distributed by MLB to fans.

Throughout the entrenched negotiations, though, two key questions have persisted: Why are the local media and salary cap issues so deeply linked, and why couldn’t owners just agree on their own to pool that revenue, similar to how the NFL operates?

The beginning of the answer lies in the accelerating economic divide between the local media revenue of well-heeled teams such as the Dodgers, Yankees, and Mets, and half the league that has lost traditional regional sports network rights deal entirely and now has its local games produced and distributed by MLB—often at less lucrative terms than what they had before.

That split, exacerbated by existential disruption across the media business, has been the key driver in a $446 million spending difference this year between the Dodgers’ total luxury-tax payroll and projected taxes, and the comparable figure for the Guardians.

The total pool of local media income in MLB has also fallen, with the roughly $2.4 billion in annual revenues earlier this decade now standing at about $1.8 billion. With a cap-based system, MLB believes it can both narrow the economic spread and enlarge the overall pie of local media revenue.

“We are trying to make changes to the game that fans want and will improve the value of our media rights,” MLB EVP of baseball operations Morgan Sword said in a presentation this week to reporters.

One of the teams whose games are produced by the league, the Brewers, won this year’s World Series, something Sword called out of step with the industry’s prevailing trends.

“It is truly aberrational in baseball for small markets to be successful,” he said. “It’s not impossible, but it is much, much more difficult in our sports than it is in any of the other sports.”

The second part of the question is more complicated. Pooling local media revenue has a direct connection to MLB’s revenue-sharing system, which is collectively bargained between the league and MLBPA due to its link to player compensation. In the current labor deal, teams currently pay 48% of their local revenue into a central pool. So the league says it cannot simply restructure this part of its economics without involving the union.

While that is indeed true, the blackouts remain a separate issue from a salary cap. A complete pooling of local media revenue, and an end to regional blackouts, could be negotiated with the union absent a salary cap, though that likely would create disruption in the current rights deals—something the league is reluctant to face.

Instead, management is seeking to achieve the local media pooling with a hard cap that players have long resisted. The league is also proposing several other sweeping changes in conjunction with the cap-and-floor system, including significant restrictions on free agency, a retooled draft, and a 154-game regular season.

“We’re not saying it’s the players’ fault there are blackouts. We’re also not saying a salary cap in isolation fixes blackouts,” Sword said. “What we are saying is that this economic system, which is a big series of trade-offs, for the clubs, for the players, enables us to do it.”

MLB additionally is looking to mimic the NBA’s recent strategy and pursue a much more nationalized strategy when its current rights deals expire after the 2028 season. The NBA did that to great success, nearly tripling its national deals to about $6.9 billion annually.

Amid all of that, the MLBPA has consistently argued that caps reduce overall player compensation, pit player against player in a zero-sum game, and erode contract covenants.

“There can be no clearer example of the league’s lack of seriousness than their insistence that they will not negotiate over the economics outside of a radical change to the system that would dramatically reduce overall player compensation for all categories of players and strip fundamental rights from players like the ability to have truly guaranteed contracts,” MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer said in a statement. “There should be no illusions about the owners’ true motivation in pushing for this system. They want to make more money in profits and franchise values by artificially suppressing player salaries.”

title: United Football League Names Allied Sports Exclusive Sponsorship Sales Agency
article_text:
ARLINGTON, TX (Nov. 19, 2026) – The United Football League today announced a multi-year agreement with Allied Sports, which will serve as the league’s exclusive national sponsorship sales partner. Allied Sports will lead efforts to identify, develop, and secure new national brand partnerships that align with the UFL’s vision, values, and long-term growth ambitions. The agreement represents an important step in building a sustainable foundation for the UFL’s long-term success, strengthening its commercial platform, and creating greater value for the brands that invest in the league.

The partnership brings together two organizations with a shared focus on storytelling and developing sponsorships that resonate with fans. Allied Sports brings a proven track record helping rightsholders sell a reason to believe and brands find a reason to belong. The agency will leverage its expertise in partnership development, brand strategy, and sponsorship sales to help identify prospective partners and create opportunities that reflect the UFL’s unique position at the intersection of professional football, entertainment, and fan engagement.

“As we continue to build momentum and scale the league, we’re focused on building meaningful partnerships with brands that connect authentically with our fans and believe in our vision for long-term success,” said UFL President & CEO Russ Brandon. “Allied Sports brings established relationships, proven experience, and strategic expertise to help us attract brands that share our ambition and can grow with us, creating lasting value for the league, its fans, and partners.”

The UFL offers brands an opportunity to participate in the evolution of a growing sports property. Under the leadership and vision of co-owner Mike Repole, the league continued to reimagine professional spring football in 2026 through on-field innovation, an emphasis on accessibility and transparency, new fan experiences, and a growing role in the football talent pipeline. Combined with audience growth and expansion into new markets, the UFL is building a platform where brands can do more than be a sponsor. They can collaborate with the UFL to help shape new experiences, reach emerging audiences, and develop distinctive partnerships as the league evolves.

“What makes the UFL compelling is the opportunity to build alongside a league that is actively shaping the future of football,” said Sean Barror, Founder and President of Allied Sports. “The UFL is a proving ground for on-field innovation, new markets, and distinctive fan experiences – all of which make for a unique storytelling platform for brands to think differently about engaging football fans. We look forward to collaborating with the league to develop creative partnerships that deliver value for UFL players, fans, and sponsors.”

The partnership comes as the UFL advances an ambitious growth strategy. Following its successful 2026 season, the league launched two new markets for 2027 in Rhode Island and Colorado and announced expansion for 2028 with new teams in Oklahoma and Utah. The growth will broaden the league’s footprint, introduce the UFL to new audiences, and create additional opportunities for national brands to engage with fans through professional spring football.

As the UFL enters new markets, each team and community will bring distinct stories, personalities, and fan experiences. Allied Sports will work with the league to translate those unique strengths into national sponsorship opportunities, connecting brand objectives with the distinctive traits of the UFL, its teams, communities, fan bases, and experiences. Together, the UFL and Allied Sports aim to build partnerships that deliver lasting value for brands while helping shape the future of professional spring football.

Those interested in partnership opportunities should reach out to Megan Fogarty, SVP Partnership Development at Allied Sports, at [email protected].

For more information on the UFL and its teams, please visit, www.theufl.com.

title: Howden Takes Irish Champion Hurdle Title Sponsorship in Three-Year Deal
article_text:
Howden has signed a three-year deal with Leopardstown Racecourse and Horse Racing Ireland to become the title sponsor of the Irish Champion Hurdle at the Dublin Racing Festival.

The first running of the Howden Irish Champion Hurdle will take place on Sunday, January 31, 2027, the second day of the festival at Leopardstown. The Grade 1 race carries a €200,000 prize fund and counts Hatton’s Grace, Istabraq, Hurricane Fly, Honeysuckle and State Man among its past winners.

The agreement comes as the global insurance broker expands its Irish business. Howden has 30 local offices across the country, providing commercial and personal insurance, financial advice and mortgages.

Mark Nolan, CEO of Howden Ireland, said the sponsorship reflected the company’s commitment to “supporting not only the equine industry, but the wider network of businesses and communities connected to it, from transport and hospitality to the many other services that help the industry thrive.”

“We are thrilled to welcome Howden as the new title sponsor of the Irish Champion Hurdle, a race steeped in history and sporting excellence,” added Rob Crabbe, Commercial Manager at HRI Racecourses.

“The Dublin Racing Festival has grown into one of the most iconic weekends in jump racing, and the Champion Hurdle is its crowning jewel on day two. Partnering with a prestigious global brand like Howden for the next three years highlights the international appeal and commercial strength of Irish racing.”

“We look forward to working closely with the Howden team to deliver an exceptional event.”

There is a clear fit between the audience at Leopardstown and the businesses Howden is looking to reach through its Irish office network.

Nolan’s reference to transport and hospitality points to where the sponsorship could do some of its best work, linking together the different strands in an industry that is also a sport, and a sport which is also a substantial industry.

Three years gives its local teams time to build relationships with the businesses that keep racing going throughout the year.

title: UEFA continues partnership spree with Würth agreement
article_text:
European soccer’s UEFA governing body has continued its recent commercial partnership spree by securing German-based fastener supplier Würth as a sponsor for its national team competitions.

The partnership covers four of UEFA’s major men’s competitions, including the flagship Euro 2028, the 2027-28 European qualifiers for the tournament, the 2027 Nations League Finals, and the 2027 European U-21 Championship, with Würth gaining a platform to increase its international visibility across Europe.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Euro 2028 is due to take place from June 9 to July 9, with matches staged across England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland.

The partnership also extends to the Euro 2028 qualification tournament, which will feature all 54 active UEFA members, giving Würth further visibility in the host countries.

Commercial appetite for the Euro 2028 tournament is ramping up. Earlier this week, alcoholic beverage conglomerate Campari Group struck a commercial partnership centered around its Aperol brand.

Meanwhile, earlier this month, Chinese payments heavyweight Ant Group’s Alipay brand renewed its coverage of UEFA tournaments for Euro 2028, and workwear company Strauss strengthened its long-standing partnership with UEFA to sponsor the tournament.

Last month, Betano, the sports betting brand owned by Kaizen Gaming, also extended its partnership with UEFA to become a Euro 2028 sponsor, while Chinese electronics brand Hisense renewed its long-running tie-up with the continental body in September to cover the tournament.

Other Euro 2028 partners announced in recent months include online travel booking platform Booking.com and BT Group, the heavyweight UK telecoms firm.

The CAA Eleven agency markets commercial rights to UEFA’s national team competitions under the current cycle but will be replaced by sports media and commercial agency Relevent after Euro 2028.

Relevent was recently awarded an eight-year contract running through 2036, covering future editions of the men's Euros in 2032 and 2036, as well as the 2029 and 2033 women's editions.

The agreement covers sponsorship sales, media rights, licensing, and other associated commercial rights.

CAA Eleven was set up in 2012 to manage the UEFA partnership.

title: FIFA confirms Diallo, Tashima to oppose Infantino in 2027 election
article_text:
The three candidates who will contest the 2027 election for FIFA president have been confirmed, with controversial incumbent Gianni Infantino facing off against France’s Philippe Diallo and Japan’s Kohzo Tashima.

The 77th FIFA Congress, where the presidential election will be held, is set to take place in Rabat, Morocco, on March 18.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Diallo is the current head of the French Football Federation (FFF), and became UEFA's surprise alternative candidate after former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, FIFA's chief of global football development, declined to run.

Tashima, meanwhile, is an honorary president of the Japan Football Association (JFA) and a member of the FIFA Council.

In a statement, FIFA said: “The candidatures have been forwarded to the electoral committee for examination and for passing a decision on the admission of the candidates.

"Member associations will be notified of the names of the proposed and admitted candidates no later than 18 February 2027."

Ramon Vega, the former soccer player for Tottenham Hotspur and Celtic, was unsurprisingly unsuccessful in his attempt to meet the requirements.

Vega was a vocal presence in recent months, but his lack of experience in soccer governance meant he was never likely to mount a sustained challenge for the presidency.

Many of soccer’s biggest national federations are united in opposing Infantino, who boasts the support of much of the world’s smaller nations, owing to his ambitious wealth distribution plans.

The Swiss-Italian’s current term runs through 2027, having been re-elected unopposed back at the FIFA congress in March 2023, meaning that if re-elected, he would stay in the role through 2031.

He was first elected in an Extraordinary Congress in 2016 following the resignation of his predecessor Sepp Blatter, and retained the role in 2019 after standing unopposed for re-election.

Infantino's leadership has been under fire in the past few months due to the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a plan revealed in July following the FIFA World Cup, through which he sought to sell off stakes in the global governing body to private investors.

The international body's plans would have involved raising $4.2 billion by selling a stake in FFE – assuming a total valuation of $20 billion in the venture.

FIFA said this would go towards creating a new funding mechanism for its 211 member associations, called the FIFA Fast-Forward Programme (FFFP).

In the months that followed the plan being shelved, European soccer's governing body UEFA and its members have been at the forefront of calls for Infantino to resign, and for there to be a leadership change at the top of FIFA.

Following on from Tashima announcing his intention to run, the JFA president, Tsuneyasu Miyamoto, added: "This decision is a major challenge to contribute to the further development of world football by utilising that experience and knowledge, and at the same time, we believe it will be an opportunity to show the world the ideals and attitudes that Japanese football has cherished."

Bidding for a fourth term heading up FIFA, Infantino told the BBC Sport outlet in October that he expects to be backed by the "vast, vast majority" of world soccer.

He made these comments following a full endorsement by the Asian Football Confederation governing body.

title: NBA adds Novig as prediction market partner; AEG joins wave with OG.com
article_text:
US basketball’s elite NBA has followed up its recent deals with Polymarket and Kalshi by adding another prediction market operator to its portfolio through a deal with Novig.

The agreement makes Novig the league’s fourth authorized prediction market partner, The Athletic has reported.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

As part of the tie-up, Novig will abide by what the NBA has described as “enhanced integrity obligations specific to prediction markets.”

The league partnered with prominent prediction market operators Polymarket and Kalshi in late October.

The NBA also expanded its partnership with fantasy sports and gaming operator DraftKings, one of its official sportsbook partners, to include prediction markets.

The agreements with Polymarket and Kalshi give the companies the right to leverage NBA data, statistics, and, perhaps crucially, NBA intellectual property (including logos and imagery) in their operations as the league’s ‘preferred prediction-market exchanges’.

In return, the league will be able to govern what NBA-related markets the pair can and cannot offer, as well as prohibit trading on NBA events by all league and team personnel, with the NBA also to collaborate with Polymarket and Kalshi for information sharing around any investigations regarding illicit and suspicious trading.

To facilitate those agreements, the NBA struck a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the regulatory body that oversees the prediction market industry) to ensure proper oversight of the prediction market business.

The NBA has followed the lead of the National Hockey League, Major League Soccer, UFC, and Major League Baseball, all of which struck agreements with Polymarket and/or Kalshi in the past year.

The NBA is, perhaps, the most prominent among all of these sports properties, and second in the US only to the NFL in terms of reach.

The NFL remains the last major men’s sports property in the US without a Polymarket or Kalshi partnership, and that may remain the case for the foreseeable future, according to comments NFL commissioner Roger Goodell made last month.

Goodell recently said that the NFL would not partner with either until there are stronger federal guardrails.

Earlier this year, Novig partnered with LIV Golf, the beleaguered international golf tour that is reportedly set to wind down its operations.

Meanwhile, Anschutz Entertainment Group (AEG), the California-based sports and entertainment company, has entered the prediction market business through a multi-property partnership with OG.com.

The tie-up makes OG.com, the prediction market and trading platform launched by Crypto.com, the exclusive prediction market platform partner for AEG’s Los Angeles sports and entertainment properties, including Crypto.com Arena, the LA Kings NHL franchise, and the LA Live entertainment district.

The partnership will combine prominent branding, digital integrations, and exclusive fan rewards.

At Crypto.com Arena, the partnership will include in-arena visibility and opportunities for OG.com to engage guests through targeted promotions, while at LA Live, the brand will be featured across the district’s digital signage network.

In addition, OG.com and the LA Kings will also introduce a series of interactive fan experiences, exclusive rewards, and special events throughout the NHL season, including OG.com being the presenting partner of an upcoming game in March at Crypto.com Arena.

The brand will also benefit from in-game visibility during LA Kings home games, including digitally enhanced and static dasherboard signage, as well as integration into social media content.

title: Skydance’s Kanal 5 and HBO Max net Ski Classic rights in Sweden
article_text:
Ski Classics, the Europe-based long-distance cross-country skiing series, has secured its visibility in Sweden after signing a new rights agreement with commercial broadcaster Kanal 5 and streaming service HBO Max.

The partnership gives Kanal 5 and HBO Max, both owned by global media conglomerate Skydance, exclusive rights in the country to the first 12 events scheduled for the Ski Classics World Championship 2026-27 season.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The season begins on December 11 and runs through April 4, with 15 events held across six countries: Austria, Switzerland, the Czech Republic, Sweden, Italy, and Norway.

The final three events of the season, the women’s and men’s Oxberg-Mora Sprint and Vasaloppet, will be aired in Sweden by public service broadcaster SVT.

Roberto Vacchi, commentator for road cycling’s elite Tour de France, will lead the pair's coverage, bringing experience from the Ski Classics.

The season will open with the Bad Gastein Prologue in Austria and end with the Grand Finale Summit 2 Senja in Norway.

The new deal comes shortly after organizers of the Ski Classics unveiled a rights extension in Finland with TV5 and HBO Max earlier this month.

The contract renewal sees the two platforms – both part of the Skydance media empire – continuing as the exclusive home in Finland for Ski Classics for the upcoming 2026-27 season.

As has been the case in previous campaigns, every event will be shown live on the HBO Max streaming platform, while most will also be available free-to-air (FTA) via linear broadcaster TV5.

title: Celsius Is Turning Sports Sponsorships Into a Year-Round Brand Platform
article_text:
Celsius is building a sports marketing system rather than betting on one big sponsorship. The energy drink brand is combining college football, Formula 1, running communities and fitness competitions to make its better-for-you positioning visible wherever active consumers already gather.

Celsius became the official energy drink sponsor of ESPN’s College GameDay in August, with campus run clubs, tailgates and a multi-year partnership. The brand also used college football NIL deals with analyst Kirk Herbstreit, Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood and Oregon quarterback Dante Moore.

The important move is not the size of any individual deal. It is the way Celsius is connecting different sports environments to the same consumer promise.

At the New York City Marathon, the brand returned with a Club Celsius pop-up and a multi-day Brooklyn takeover. It also sponsored Diplo’s Run Club stops in New York, Chicago and Los Angeles. Earlier in the year, Celsius became the official global energy drink partner of the ATHX Games, a fitness competition.

That gives Live. Fit. Go., the 360-degree campaign launched in 2025 across television, paid and organic social, out-of-home and experiential marketing, more places to show up. A runner, college football fan and Formula 1 viewer may not share a sport, but they can still recognize the same brand behavior: Celsius is present around performance, movement and the rituals that surround them.

Celsius is also extending the strategy into premium global sports. The company signed British driver Jessica Hawkins ahead of the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix and continues its multi-year partnership with Aston Martin Aramco in Formula 1.

That range is deliberate. Celsius CMO Kyle Watson told Modern Retail that the brand is not defined by a single sport and wants to build connections across the sports landscape. The approach gives Celsius more chances to meet consumers in context, rather than asking one event or athlete to carry the entire brand story.

There is a practical lesson here for marketers. Sports sponsorship works harder when it creates repeatable participation around the rights deal: a run club, a campus activation, a fan event or a product ritual. The logo may create awareness, but the surrounding behavior gives the partnership a reason to be remembered.

Celsius is effectively using sports as a year-round distribution network for its positioning. The strategic consequence is that future growth will depend less on adding famous names and more on making each new partnership feel like another credible expression of the same active lifestyle.

title: Sponsor spotlight: McLaren F1 gives Velo a global audience
DFB taps Sportfive for rights distribution in the US
article_text:
German soccer’s DFB governing body has hired international sports marketing agency Sportfive to market and distribute its media rights in the US.

Under the partnership, Sportfive will launch the German Soccer Network, the DFB’s FAST (Free-Ad-Supported-Streaming TV) channel, exclusively on LG Smart TVs across the US, giving users live and on-demand coverage of the DFB-Pokal domestic cup competition, live third-division matches, live youth national team matches, and original and archival programming.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

As part of the agreement, Sportfive aided the DFB in securing LG as the exclusive US distribution partner for the German Soccer Network, with LG viewers also gaining access to select standalone live broadcasts of DFB-Pokal matches.

The service is available immediately and will include live coverage of DFB-Pokal’s Round of 16, including matches involving Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich on December 1 and Borussia Dortmund on December 2.

Beyond German Soccer Network, Sportfive will also look for opportunities that expand access to DFB competitions and content while connecting new audiences with the German game.

Adam Schneider, head of US Media at Sportfive, said: “This partnership reflects Sportfive’s ability to connect world-class rights holders with innovative media distribution opportunities.

“By bringing the German Soccer Network to LG Channels, we’re helping DFB reach new audiences in the United States and making German football more accessible than ever for fans across the country.”

DFB’s programming will sit alongside German soccer’s other media partnerships in the country, including Versant, the spin-off division of US media giant NBCUniversal (NBCU), which secured an exclusive five-season English-speaking rights agreement, running from the 2026-27 to 2030-31 campaigns.

The rights package, reportedly worth $100 million in total, includes Versant airing over 300 games live per season of the 18-team league, through cable channel USA Network and the Fandango platform.

Specifically, at least 30 games will be shown via USA Network, while the others will stream free-to-air on Fandango to prioritize reach.

NBCUniversal’s Telemundo, meanwhile, holds exclusive Spanish-language rights to air over 100 of the 306 Bundesliga matches across its Telemundo and Universo linear channels, as well as streaming service Peacock, as part of its three-year deal that started with the current 2026-27 season.

Lasse Eckartsberg, head of international media rights at DFB, added: “As international rights owners navigate an evolving media landscape in the US and globally, DFB is looking beyond traditional media rights opportunities.

“Sportfive are the right partner to support us in this exciting endeavor of unlocking new commercial potential together with LG and growing our audience and market presence in the United States.”

The new deal comes as the DFB looks to expand its presence in the US on the back of increased fandom after the country co-hosted the flagship FIFA World Cup alongside Canada and Mexico earlier this year.

The Americas is a major target region for the Bundesliga, which has succeeded in growing its presence in the region over the past few years, evidenced by the league’s Spanish-language Instagram and TikTok accounts, which boast a combined follower count of over 548,500.

Over the past five years, the Bundesliga claims that its fanbase in the US has grown by 43%.

In all, nine players from the US currently ply their trade in the Bundesliga, including national team stalwarts Malik Tillman at Bayer Leverkusen and Giovanni Reyna at Borussia Mönchengladbach.

title: Kenya is ready to host 2027 HSBC SEVENS 2,says PS Mwangi
article_text:
Sports Principal Secretary Elijah Mwangi has reaffirmed the country’s commitment to host the 2027 leg of the HSBC World Rugby Sevens Division Two series in Nairobi.

The PS said this today when he hosted a high-level World Rugby delegation led by Mark Honeybunn, Head of Event and Planning Delivery for Sevens, for discussions on Kenya’s readiness to host HSBC SVNS 2 in January 2027.

The 2027 HSBC SVNS 2 series will open with the Kenyan leg between 23rd and 24th January at the Raila Odinga international stadium.

It will be followed by the 2nd leg in Montevideo-Uruguay on the 20th and 21st of February before culminating with the final series in São Paulo, Brazil, from the 27th to the 28th of February.

“Hosting a tournament of this stature is a significant statement of Kenya’s growing standing in international sports. It reflects the confidence placed in our country to stage high-profile global competitions while opening up opportunities for tourism, investment, job creation, sports development, and international visibility.” PS added

“It is also an opportunity to showcase Kenya’s hospitality, organizational capacity, and sporting ambition to the world.” PS Mwangi continued.

PS Mwangi recognized the vital role and privileges that come alongside staging international sports events.

“We have the passion, the facilities, and the ambition to position Kenya as a leading hub for international sporting events. As a government, we remain committed to strengthening sports infrastructure, nurturing talent, supporting athletes, and unlocking the economic potential of sports,” noted PS Mwangi

The meeting was also attended by senior officials, including Director General Sports Kenya Timothy Kilimo, Secretary of Administration Josephine Ouko, Director of Sports Bernard Ouma, and Kenya Rugby Union top officials led by President Harriet Akech.

Kenya’s Shujaa will participate in the SVNS 2 series next year as it seeks to earn promotion to the core sevens series after falling in the last hurdle in this year’s qualification.

title: Cricket Australia adds Audoo partnership as sandpaper scandal rumbles on
article_text:
The Cricket Australia governing body has announced a new commercial agreement with UK music technology company Audoo as it continues to deal with the fallout over revelations concerning its team’s ball-tampering saga from 2018.

Under the new deal, Audoo will deliver automated real-time music recognition and reporting services for CA’s international series and domestic Big Bash competitions.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Specifically, CA will utilize Audoo’s Audio Meters to recognise and analyse music used across all match formats, at stadiums and grounds across the country, providing unique insights to support the governing body’s fan engagement strategy.

Cricket Australia acting general manager, events & operations Jacqui Ward said: “Music is a vital part of our match day experience; it adds impact and engages our fans.

“Our team has long been a leader in adopting new technologies, and we are thoroughly impressed with Audoo’s solution and how easily this can be integrated into our processes.”

Audoo said the partnership is the first in several global sporting deals it has secured after deploying and testing their solution across major stadiums and sporting events over the past year.

Audoo’s chief commercial officer Matthew Fackrell said: “We are extremely pleased to be working with Cricket Australia to deliver accurate music reporting that will ensure the artists and songwriters played to the hundreds of thousands of fans in the stadiums and cricket grounds can be recognized and receive the appropriate royalty payments.

“Cricket Australia have been a pleasure to work with, and our team continues to be impressed by their willingness to embrace our solution and unlock all the benefits that our data insights can provide.”

The new deal comes as Cricket Australia contends with new explosive revelations made by former Test cricketer Cameron Bancroft, who today claimed the entire Australia team knew about the use of sandpaper during the 2018 tour of South Africa, contrary to previous statements made by players.

The scandal was reignited this month after the release of Usman Khawaja’s book that claimed that knowledge of the cheating went beyond the three players who were punished for their part.

Writing in a column published by the West Australian newspaper, Bancroft said he was responding to a conference given by current captain Pat Cummins rebuffing Khawaja’s account in Sydney.

He said: “It was not just the three of us – Steve Smith, David Warner and I – who knew about me using sandpaper on the ball in South Africa. It was the whole team.

“The final straw for me to write this account was Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins' press conference. It made me feel angry, betrayed and alone.

“What I saw, experienced and lived with – not only him, but everyone else on that tour in South Africa – is not the public account he gave in his press conference and in the years previously when he has spoken on this time."

Bancroft’s column was published just hours after Cricket Australia announced an independent forum to explore the scandal, giving players the opportunity to share their version of events without fears of retrospective punishment.

In a statement, CA said: “We respect that Cameron Bancroft has told his story, and we will take time to consider his comments.

"We expect that there will be many dimensions to the events of 2018, which is why we have established the forum for individuals to give their version of events.

"We are finalizing the terms of reference and will commence the process as soon as possible."

The new revelations will heap pressure on Pat Cummins, the Australian team, and CA, whose independent forum will now come under scrutiny, given that it has stated it will not re-prosecute on the back of new information.

Commenting on the reputational damage, Olivia Snooks, analyst at GlobalData Sport, said: “Cricket Australia’s sponsors will be watching closely. After the 2018 scandal, several partners, including Magellan, walked away.

“New allegations involving captain Pat Cummins, the playing group, and coaching staff risk reviving those integrity concerns just as the home Test summer begins.

“While the full financial fallout remains unclear, the longer this controversy drags on, the more likely current sponsors will pull back, and prospective ones will delay new deals.”

LVSportsBiz Digest: Apparently, F1 Still Has Las Vegas Grand Prix Tickets To Sell; VGK Renew Ten-Year Naming Rights For City National Arena To 2037
article_text:
By Alan Snel, LVSportsBiz.com Publisher-Writer

LAS VEGAS, Nevada — At last week’s Las Vegas tourism board meeting, LVCVA CEO Steve Hill said the Las Vegas Grand Prix was sold out and 175,000 Formula 1 visitors would be coming to Las Vegas for the annual November sports events Thursday to Saturday.

For a sports event that is supposedly sold out, it was rather newsworthy that F1 Las Vegas emailed LVSportsBiz.com ticket information that there were still tickets available to purchase.

Saturday’ two-hour race features car racers driving open-wheel vehicles on the 3.8-mile course that follows Las Vegas Boulevard, Harmon Avenue, Koval Lane and Sands Avenue.

The Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority (LVCVA), the publicly-funded government agency that promotes the Strip, says the event brings in high-paying fans who spend more than the average Las Vegas tourist.

The race also keeps non-race visitors away from Strip, limits access to local businesses along the race route and causes traffic jams in the Strip corridor.

Clark County commissioners give permission to the Liberty Media-owned F1 to take over roads in the Strip corridor and turn them into a linear outdoor stadium for fans to watch the fast cars and consume food and drinks.

The Las Vegas Grand Prix does not pay Clark County money to take over public roads. Instead, the publicly-funded LVCVA pays $100 million in “sponsorship” money to the Las Vegas Grand Prix to have the race until 2037. The race invites local middle school students to tour the pit lanes, handed out award to students who did F1 artwork and gave 14 UNLV hospitality course students a behind-the-scenes look at the race. F1 has tried to connect with Las Vegas after a disastrous first race in 2023 when the grand prix event staged the race without community reach out.

The Vegas Golden Knights’ training center in Summerlin will be called City National Arena for another ten years through 2037 thanks to a naming rights sponsorship deal that has been renewed between VGK owner Bill Foley and City National Bank.

Officially speaking, RBC City National Bank will remain the “Official Bank Partner” of the Vegas Golden Knights.

The Golden Knights return to action Thursday when the NHL teams hosts the Dallas Stars for a second straight game T-Mobile Arena.

The MLB A’s, scheduled to start play in Las Vegas in 2028, have a new pitching coach nd a new hitting coach.

Casey Weathers will join the A’s as pitching coach and Trevor Amicone will join the A’s as hitting coach on manager Mark Kotsay’s coaching staff for the 2027 season — if there is a MLB season.

Weathers, a native of Elk Grove, Calif., spent the last two seasons as the director of pitching development for the Philadelphia Phillies.

Originally selected by the Rockies out of Vanderbilt in the first round of the 2007 First-Year Player Draft, Weathers spent 10 seasons in minor league baseball with Colorado, Chicago-NL, Tampa Bay, and Cleveland.

Amicone served as the assistant hitting coach for the Minnesota Twins from 2025-26 after spending five seasons as a hitting coach in the New York Yankees system, including serving as the hitting coach for Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre from 2022-24.

The Las Vegas Marathon returns Jan. 10 for its third annual event and will debut a new course that brings the full marathon distance back to Las Vegas Boulevard.

title: Snapdragon Bets On F1's Youngest-Ever Champion To Sharpen Sports Marketing Returns For Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM)
article_text:
When Kimi Antonelli claimed the Formula 1 World Championship title this month at just 20 years old, chipmaker Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM) already had him under contract.

Qualcomm’s consumer-facing brand Snapdragon had signed Antonelli as a brand ambassador, a move now anchored by a new anthem film timed to the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix on November 21.

The campaign marks a deliberate shift in how Qualcomm approaches sports sponsorship, prioritizing measurable returns over the prestige-driven partnerships the company pursued in previous years.

Snapdragon’s current deal with the Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula 1 team, of which Antonelli is a driver, launched in 2023 and was built from the outset around marketing accountability.

That contrasts sharply with Qualcomm’s earlier Mercedes partnership from the 2010s, which CMO Don McGuire acknowledged was not “ROI-driven, marketing-driven” in its orientation.

McGuire, who took the CMO role in 2021, is now overseeing a strategy that extends the brand relationship from content and storytelling into activations and hospitality.

“We believe we’re already seeing higher ROI coming out of some things that we’ve done in the short term,” McGuire said, signaling confidence in the retooled approach.

One structural challenge facing the campaign is Apple TV’s exclusive U.S. broadcast rights to F1, which blocks brands like Snapdragon from placing traditional television ads around domestic race coverage.

Rather than treating that as a ceiling, the brand is routing the anthem film through Sky broadcasts outside the United States, alongside digital placements and partnerships with Sports Illustrated and YouTube.

“We’ve got other ways to bring it to life,” McGuire said of the campaign’s distribution strategy around the Las Vegas race.

Antonelli’s historic championship adds significant organic reach to the partnership, as the Italian driver’s record-breaking season has drawn sustained global media attention throughout the year.

Snapdragon’s sports marketing ambitions extend well beyond the paddock, with the brand also holding a sponsorship deal with what McGuire describes as the world’s biggest soccer property.

That soccer partnership has generated what McGuire called “humongous ROI,” and it now serves as the internal benchmark against which all other sports deals are measured.

“When you’re dealing with a sports brand that big, at scale, the brand can withstand the ebbs and flows of performance on the pitch because the fan base is so huge,” McGuire explained.

He added: “That’s the benchmark that we use [for sports partnerships] and maybe it’s a little unfair because they are arguably the biggest sports brand in the world.”

The Antonelli signing reflects a broader industry trend of brands pursuing younger, generationally resonant athletes as Formula 1 continues expanding its commercial footprint in North America.

title: NASCAR Lands Major Sponsorship Deal for 2027 Chase Race
article_text:
Watkins Glen International is getting a new race sponsor to go along with its return to NASCAR's championship stretch.

The New York road course announced Monday that Busch Light will serve as the entitlement sponsor of its 2027 NASCAR Cup Series race, officially naming the event Busch Light at The Glen.

https://twitter.com/WGI/status/2122435803120832560

Scheduled for Sunday, Sept. 19, the race will hold particular significance on next season's calendar. Watkins Glen will be the only road course featured in the 2027 NASCAR Chase, putting a premium on road racing talent as drivers compete for the Cup Series championship.

For Busch Light, the agreement gives one of NASCAR's most recognizable commercial partners an even greater presence during the most consequential portion of the season.

Few beer brands have as deep a history in stock car racing as Busch.

A longtime supporter of the sport, Busch Light currently serves as a Premier Partner and the Official Beer Sponsor of NASCAR. The brand also sponsors the Busch Light Pole Award, giving it a consistent presence throughout the Cup Series season.

Its latest investment puts the brand's name on one of the most anticipated road course races of 2027.

"Busch Light has been part of NASCAR race weekends for decades, and we're proud to deepen that connection as entitlement partner of Busch Light at The Glen," said Krystyn Stowe, head of marketing, Busch Family & Natural Family at Anheuser-Busch.

The financial terms of the sponsorship were not disclosed in the announcement.

After hosting its Cup Series race in May in 2026, Watkins Glen will return to a fall race date next season with considerably more at stake.

As the lone road course on the Chase schedule, the 2.45-mile circuit presents a vastly different challenge for championship contenders accustomed to competing on ovals.

"With The Glen returning to The Chase in 2027, we're proud to build on our road racing tradition together and welcome fans to the Finger Lakes for a fall weekend with championship stakes," Watkins Glen International President Dawn Burlew said.

- Friday, Sept. 17: ARCA Menards Series race

- Saturday, Sept. 18: NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series Mission Foods 200 at The Glen

- Sunday, Sept. 19: NASCAR Cup Series Busch Light at The Glen

Tickets and camping packages for the 2027 race weekend are already on sale through Watkins Glen International.

For the New York circuit, a nationally recognized title sponsor and a race with championship implications make for a particularly attractive combination heading into 2027.

article_text:
Ticketing and entertainment tech provider Fever has entered into a deal with heavyweight esports organization Blast, running through 2029.

Through a tie-up unveiled today, Fever becomes the esports organization's exclusive ticketing partner across its entire live events portfolio.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Fever will work to integrate ticket searches, purchasing, transfers, and event access into one platform.

Fever's technology will be integrated into the various Blast online platforms, while tickets will also be sold through Fever's sales channels.

In addition, Fever will provide Blast with on-site ticketing operations, including "secure access-control technology and box-office terminals, alongside 24/7 multilingual customer support."

Marketing and promotion will also be provided by Fever through the deal.

Overall, this forms part of the wider Blast efforts to ramp up the live events side of its business.

James Woollard, Blast's vice president of destinations and marketing, commented: "Partnering with Fever allows us to bring more of that journey together in one place, making it easier for fans to discover our events, buy with confidence, securely resell or transfer tickets and personalise their experience after purchase.”

title: EHF’s rights sales model shows early results with deals in 80 territories
article_text:
EHF Marketing’s in-house media distribution strategy is paying early dividends, with the commercial arm of the European Handball Federation growing its existing network of rights agreements globally.

Through existing and new agreements, the EHF Champions League and EHF European League club competitions will be broadcast across 80 territories worldwide in the 2026-27 season.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

EHF Marketing took direct responsibility for the rights management, broadcaster servicing, production, distribution, and content services of its club competitions from the 2026-27 season onwards after the governing body prematurely ended its 10-year contract with sports marketing agency Infront late last year.

The continental body has secured several new media rights agreements across key European markets, the Middle East and North Africa, and the US.

These agreements complement the EHF’s established international broadcast network, including existing partnerships with Viaplay, AMC, Arena Sport and Polsat, among others.

The deals cover a range of distribution channels, including traditional broadcasters, OTT (over-the-top, or streaming) platforms, and club-owned media channels.

EHF Marketing stated that the new agreements “reflect different distribution models and market needs and demonstrate a flexible, market-specific approach to media rights exploitation, taking into consideration broadcaster structures and strategic objectives.”

Key agreements include a recently announced long-term partnership with sports streaming platform Dyn Sports covering Germany, Austria and Switzerland, with matches distributed via its OTT platform. There will also be OTT distribution of matches in Iceland, via Livey.

In France, the competitions will be shown on BeIN Sports, the international pay-TV broadcaster, and Handball TV, the jointly owned OTT platform from the French Handball Federation and the domestic top-flight LNH.

In Spain, TV3 will offer free-to-air (FTA) coverage of Barcelona matches, while all competitions and matches are also available on EHFTV.

Meanwhile, in Portugal, Sporting CP, FC Porto, and Benfica are distributing their matches through club-owned media channels, complementing broadcasts on Sport TV.

In Switzerland, the Swiss Broadcasting Corporation (SRG SSR) will provide FTA coverage of selected matches while MSG Networks will broadcast selected EHF Champions League games in the US.

EHF Marketing claims its direct rights management model has enabled it to gain “greater commercial and strategic flexibility.”

Aurèle Weyeneth, director rights and exploitation at EHF Marketing, said: “Actively managing media rights in-house gives us more flexibility in how we approach each market, both commercially and strategically.

“Our objective is not simply to sign more agreements, but to find the right distribution partners and make our competitions as accessible as possible to handball fans. Whether through traditional broadcasters, OTT platforms or club media channels, each market has its own specificities, and these new agreements reflect our approach.”

Elsewhere, France Télévisions, the domestic public-service broadcaster, has agreed a deal with the French Handball Federation for rights to broadcast the national women's team matches for the EHF Euro 2026 tournament.

From December 11, France Télévisions will broadcast the four main round matches on its channels, along with the semi-final and the final, should France qualify.

Philippe Bana, president of the French Handball Federation, said: “In January, we made the decision to take control of handball media rights to offer our men’s national team the widest possible visibility. We are proud to extend this approach to our women’s national team.

“With BeIN Sports, a long-standing partner of French handball, and France Télévisions, which is reaffirming its commitment to us, the French women’s team will benefit from exposure commensurate with its achievements and the public’s affection.

“Seeing both our French national teams accessible to the general public in the same year sends a strong message for handball, our members, and our partners.”

title: IOC seeks new South Korean broadcast partner as JTBC drops Olympic rights
article_text:
JTBC, the debt-ridden South Korean broadcaster, has terminated its rights agreement with the International Olympic Committee (IOC) covering the Winter and Summer Games through 2032 as part of its rehabilitation plan.

In a statement, JTBC said it hoped the move would “eliminate financial uncertainty and establish a stable management foundation,” adding that it would “continue to communicate closely with the IOC through various channels to address outstanding matters arising from the termination of the agreement,” including remaining broadcast rights fees.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The company said it expects another broadcaster or consortium to secure the rights for the remaining events on the contract, including the upcoming 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, the 2030 Alps Winter Olympics, and the 2032 Brisbane Olympics.

The broadcaster added: “The costs resulting from the termination will be determined through the third quarter accounting process and in accordance with the rehabilitation plan once it is approved.

“By accounting for the expected losses as part of the rehabilitation process, we aim to remove financial uncertainty and sustain growth in operating profit from our core businesses.”

JTBC secured exclusive broadcasting rights covering four Olympic events between 2026 and 2032 after securing a contract with the IOC in June 2019.

The broadcaster had initially planned to resell its Olympic rights to major Korean broadcasters, but negotiations broke down, leaving JTBC to bear the cost of solely broadcasting the games.

JTBC also picked up exclusive rights in the country to soccer’s flagship World Cups between 2026 and 2030 in a deal reportedly worth $250 million. The agreement covers the 2030 edition of the men's soccer tournament and the FIFA Women's World Cup in 2027.

Sublicensing this year’s World Cup also faced difficulties, but KBS eventually agreed to purchase rights to jointly air the tournament.

The financial burden of both rights contracts ultimately led to the company filing for corporate rehabilitation proceedings with the Seoul Bankruptcy Court last June.

In August, a Seoul court approved the broadcaster’s request to begin rehabilitation proceedings, allowing the company to restructure its debts under court supervision.

Earlier this month, JTBC officially started the company’s sale process, with the aim of selecting a preferred bidder in January.

title: In 2026,WNBA generated $608 million in sponsor value, with Caitlin Clark’s Indiana Fever driving $205 mil
article_text:
The WNBA generated an estimated $608 million in sponsor media value during the 2026 regular season, a 53.9 per cent increase on the previous year, according to a new report from Relo Metrics. The figures reveal how much national television exposure, the league’s expanding broadcast partnerships and the popularity of Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever are contributing to the commercial value of women’s basketball. But the findings also show that brands do not necessarily need a league-wide agreement to benefit, with several team-level partnerships producing substantial returns.

The WNBA generated $608 million in Sponsor Media Value (SMV) during the 2026 regular season, up 53.9 per cent year on year, according to the 2026 WNBA Regular Season Sponsorship Report released by Relo Metrics on November 12. The figure measures the estimated value of brand exposure across broadcasts and social media, rather than the amount of money paid to the league through sponsorship contracts.

Broadcast exposure accounted for more than $545 million, approximately 90 per cent of the total, while social media contributed nearly $63 million. Broadcast media value increased by 62 per cent compared with the previous season, making television and other broadcast coverage the principal source of the league’s sponsorship value.

The increase coincided with the first year of the WNBA’s new 11-year media rights agreement, which brought NBC, NBC Sports and USA Network into the league’s broadcast portfolio. Those new partners contributed $105 million in Sponsor Media Value, according to

That represents roughly 19 per cent of the $545 million generated through broadcast exposure.

The report also found that the value was concentrated among a relatively small group of major partners. Michelob Ultra, Nike, State Farm, Coinbase and Tampax collectively generated nearly $247 million in Sponsor Media Value, accounting for approximately 41 per cent of the league-wide total. Their combined figure illustrates the commercial advantage available to brands with prominent league-level agreements, although the findings also identify opportunities for companies working directly with individual teams.

Relo Metrics is an artificial intelligence-powered sports sponsorship intelligence platform and a division of GumGum, a technology company specialising in advertising and contextual intelligence. Its platform measures brand exposure across live sports broadcasts, social media and streaming, helping sponsors, teams and leagues assess the visibility and estimated media value of their partnerships.

“The WNBA offers several ways for brands to reach basketball fans,” said Ryan Meizinger, Director of Insights and Strategic Services at Relo Metrics. “While league partnerships remain the strongest guarantee to capitalize on women’s basketball, it is a team’s schedule and the placement of a logo that shapes the value of the partnership. Good team deals can put brands in front of national audiences.”

The Indiana Fever were one of the clearest examples of how a team’s national profile can influence the commercial value of the league. The franchise generated $205 million in broadcast Sponsor Media Value, accounting for approximately 37.6 per cent of the WNBA’s $545 million broadcast total.

The figure is particularly notable because the Fever played in only 13 per cent of the league’s regular-season games. They were also the only team whose every game was shown nationally, giving sponsors attached to the franchise repeated access to a much wider television audience than teams without the same level of coverage.

Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark celebrates during the second half in Game 2 of a WNBA basketball first-round playoff series against the Las Vegas Aces in Indianapolis, Tuesday, Sept. 29, 2026. (AP Photo/Michael Conroy)

Caitlin Clark’s profile has been central to the Fever’s visibility, with her performances and the attention surrounding the team helping attract viewers across the season. The report also found that Clark and the Fever dominated social media value, although the commercial growth was not limited to Indianapolis.

The other 14 teams collectively generated $48 million in full media value through their social media posts, alongside 101 million engagements. That figure points to the value of team-owned content outside live broadcasts, including player photographs, video clips, behind-the-scenes material, Instagram reels and question-and-answer sessions that give supporters more direct access to players.

Uniforms were particularly effective in extending sponsorship exposure onto social platforms. They generated more than $40 million in social media value, with social accounting for 39 per cent of the uniforms’ total value. In practical terms, a sponsor’s logo could continue appearing in player photographs and video content long after a game had ended, adding another source of visibility beyond television coverage.

Across all sponsorship assets, the floor court logo, baseline apron signage and uniforms were the three most valuable placements. Together, they generated 53 per cent of the WNBA’s total Sponsor Media Value. The findings indicate that where a brand appears can be as important as the size of its partnership, particularly when an asset is repeatedly visible during nationally televised games or reproduced through social media content.

The report also identified a relationship between team performance and sponsorship exposure. Seven of the eight teams leading the SMV rankings had winning records during the season. Relo Metrics suggested that successful teams could be better positioned to secure more national primetime appearances in 2027, creating further opportunities for their commercial partners.

Although the five leading league sponsors accounted for approximately 41 per cent of the total value, Relo Metrics found that brands could generate substantial exposure through agreements with individual franchises. Around 85 brands recorded at least $1 million in Sponsor Media Value during the season, demonstrating that the commercial opportunities extended well beyond the league’s biggest partnerships.
