London Stadium: Khan ‘failed miserably’ over West Ham naming rights deal
article_text:
Mayor of London Sadiq Khan has been accused of “failing miserably” in his attempt to sell the naming rights for West Ham United’s London Stadium.

The former Olympic arena is a decade into a long-term deal with Championship club West Ham but remains without a headline sponsor despite its existence costing the taxpayer £20m per year.

And while Khan’s chief of staff David Bellamy told the London Assembly that City Hall continues “to be in the marketplace” and that “there are some discussions that are happening”, he cited West Ham’s summer relegation from the Premier League and the general market as obstacles to recruiting a sponsor.

Conservative leader Susan Hall has hit back, however, saying: “The Mayor has had a decade in office to sell the sponsorship rights to one of the country’s most iconic stadiums, and has failed miserably.

“Instead, taxpayers are left on the hook for the costs, because Lord Khan has inexplicably failed to market a world-class former-Olympic asset to businesses keen to be associated with London or sport. It beggars belief.”

The London Stadium is primarily used for football but also stages athletics and concerts, with the local council this week granting permission for the stadium to host more live music.

The arena has been at the centre of a rumoured sale storm with Amanda Staveley, the former Newcastle United shareholder, recently declaring her interest in buying a stake in West Ham and developing the land around the stadium.

But City Hall has since confirmed that there had been no bid to buy the stadium – from the current owners or elsewhere – despite a reported £50m price tag.

West Ham’s largest stakeholder is Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky, owner of Royal Mail, while David Sullivan holds around 40 per cent of the club’s shares. The latter stepped down from his board role despite denying historic allegations of inappropriate behaviour that were lodged against him last season.

A London Stadium spokesperson said: “London Stadium has not stood still over the past decade. We have continued to develop the venue, improve operational efficiency, invest in its infrastructure and build a portfolio of major sporting and entertainment events, while navigating some complex commercial and contractual arrangements.

“The recent planning approval from Newham Council demonstrates that we are looking firmly ahead. Increasing our allocation of non-sporting events from 10 to 24 creates a significant opportunity to grow our commercial revenues, attract more world-class events and deliver further economic benefits for East London.”

title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
article_text:
The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.

Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry.

There also appears to be a clear frontrunner. “I would put money on Netflix to win – they will pay whatever it takes,” one experienced media rights buyer told the Guardian.

Multiple sources have confirmed that Netflix would submit a bid before Thursday’s deadline for first-round offers, along with their fellow streamers Apple TV, Disney, Amazon, YouTube and Dazn, as well as the traditional broadcasting heavyweights, Fox, ESPN, NBC Universal and Skydance, although the last of these may find itself constrained by the budget cuts being made after its $110bn acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery. Netflix has already bought exclusive rights in the US for the 2027 and 2031 Women’s World Cups.

“There’s a huge range of buyers and therefore a broad range of possible outcomes,” one broadcasting veteran says. “All the media companies and streamers will bid. Fox will find it very challenging to retain the rights.”

In a significant change, Fifa is selling the English and Spanish rights together for the first time, a move that indicates it is seeking a single exclusive rights holder, which would suit the streaming companies. With Fox having paid $485m for exclusive English-language rights to the 2026 World Cup, and NBC Universal’s Telemundo paying $600m for the Spanish-language rights, the only certainty is that the 2030 price will be far higher, despite less attractive kick-off times for a US audience as the tournament is in Morocco, Spain and Portugal.

The impact of the time difference is hard to price, but may not prove to be that significant given the seemingly insatiable demand. NBC paid about $1.5bn for exclusive rights for the 2024 Paris Olympics and were rewarded with average daily viewing figures of more than 30 million, albeit with far more variation in programming than a World Cup.

Fifa awarded non-competitive extensions to Fox and Telemundo in 2015 as compensation for moving the 2022 Qatar World Cup to winter, a perspective that was strengthened on the back of this year’s record-breaking tournament. Fox’s live coverage of Spain’s extra-time victory over Argentina in the final was the most-watched soccer telecast in US history, with a peak audience of 51.685 million; five World Cup games brought in average audiences of more than 20 million; and the average viewing figure across all 104 matches was 7.7 million, twice the figure in Qatar four years earlier.

Telemundo’s coverage, available through NBC’s streaming platform Peacock, averaged a total audience of 6 million viewers per game, with Spain v Argentina and Mexico v England attracting peak audiences of more than 23 million, the highest-ever for Spanish-language broadcasts in the US.

The bumper audiences were extremely lucrative for the broadcasters, with figures from the advertising sales analysts Guideline showing that Fox and Telemundo generated a combined $1.19bn in advertising revenue alone during the tournament, almost three times the figure from Qatar four years earlier and more than their original rights investment.

Fox alone brought in $835m from World Cup advertising, with 30-second slots costing between $200,000 and $750,000 according to the Hollywood Reporter, and the six-minute hydration breaks generating between $2m and $9m per game.

Having left a considerable amount of money on the table because of the circumstances of the 2026 process, Fifa is determined to cash in this time around. Holding the auction only four months after the US hosted the World Cup appears a clear attempt to capitalise on the success of the previous tournament, which contributed the vast majority of Fifa’s $4bn media revenues over the four-year cycle to 2026.

The addition of hydration breaks will give bidders such as Fox more revenue to play with, although Fifa will expect the option for extra adverts to drive up the price and take its own cut this time around, having missed out in the summer. The two three-minute breaks in each half were only finalised last year and did not feature in the 2026 tender documents.

“Sports advertising is much more valuable than entertainment programming as it has a broader reach,” says François Godard, an independent media analyst. “And one-off events such as World Cups do not generally do particularly well for subscription services, who want year-round content.

“Fox in particular needs the World Cup and is heavily associated with it. They are the smallest of the legacy broadcasters and are reliant on sport, as well as news. Having said that, the market for sport amongst streamers is far more competitive in the US than in Europe. Netflix, Amazon and YouTube have all bought NFL rights, while Apple is investing heavily in Formula One, so I wouldn’t rule any of them out.”

Adam Kelly, president of the global sports marketing agency IMG, has a seat at the table at many rights negotiations and has long predicted the rise of the streamers, viewing the 2030 World Cup as the potential tipping point when a premium event could be exclusively bought in a major market by a streaming service for the first time. IMG has the rights to sell more than 70 global sports organisations, including the Premier League, World Rugby and Wimbledon.

title: DAZN adds WatchAFL, WatchNRL to global sports offering
article_text:
Global sports OTT platform DAZN has announced a deal to carry WatchAFL and WatchNRL, the international streaming services for the Australian Football League (AFL) and National Rugby League (NRL), respectively.

Through the agreements, the men’s AFL and the women’s AFLW competitions and the NRL and NRLW will be available across DAZN’s 200 markets.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

WatchAFL and WatchNRL were previously operated by Foxtel Group, which holds Australian broadcast and streaming rights to both properties and is part of DAZN’s global platform following its acquisition of Foxtel in April 2025.

International viewers will have access to every match of the 2027 AFL Premiership Season and Finals Series, alongside the AFLW, AFL Origin, the AAMI Community Series, select classic matches, and AFL news and entertainment programming.

The launch on DAZN comes ahead of the 2026 AFLW Grand Final, which takes place on November 27.

The 2027 AFL Origin match will see Western Australia take on South Australia at Optus Stadium in Perth on 27 February, ahead of the AFL Premiership Season commencing in mid-March, with the opening round featuring all 18 clubs in a traditional nine-game round of football fixtures across the country.

Meanwhile, WatchNRL will provide coverage of the 2027 NRL Premiership, including the Finals and pre-season, alongside the State of Origin Series, the NRL Women’s Premiership, select classic matches and news and entertainment programming from Fox League.

The 2027 Premiership season kicks off at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on February 27 (local time), with Melbourne Storm taking on Wests Tigers and Parramatta Eels facing Gold Coast Titans.

The AFL and NRL’s OTT offerings join DAZN’s portfolio of global sports and competitions, including FIFA+, NFL Game Pass, NHL.TV, Courtside 1891 (FIBA basketball) and Rally TV.

Andrew Dillon, AFL CEO, said: “The passion for Australian football extends well beyond Australia. Bringing WatchAFL onto DAZN’s global platform makes that connection easier, while also giving both the AFL and AFLW an even greater opportunity to reach new audiences and introduce our game to sports fans around the world.

“We’re incredibly proud of our game and ambitious about its international reach. This partnership is another important step in taking Australian football to more people in more places.”

Peter V’landys AM, executive chairman of the Australian Rugby League Commission, added: “Rugby League is made for the world stage. The pace and physicality of the game and the passion of our fans resonate wherever it's seen, and WatchNRL’s launch on DAZN gives us a brilliant new platform to showcase that to fans globally.

“We want to grow rugby league, reach new audiences, and ensure the game is accessible to more fans than ever before. Placing WatchNRL alongside some of the world’s biggest sporting competitions gives us the platform to achieve that.”

title: Betano announces suspension of master sponsorship deal with Flamengo
article_text:
Betano, Flamengo’s master sponsor, formalized the suspension of its agreement with the Rio de Janeiro club this Tuesday (17th). The decision was made as a result of Provisional Measure 1,394/2026, which banned sports betting and online gambling in Brazil.

According to an official statement, the brand announced that the move was necessary “given the continued uncertainty surrounding the sector” and the “lack of a definitive ruling” on the provisional measure.

Betano also emphasized that it sought to adapt to the situation, “focusing on preserving jobs and maintaining its commitments to social projects and to the club,” as well as keeping the sponsorship in place for as long as possible, both in football and Olympic sports.

However, the persistence of this scenario led the company to suspend the sponsorship “until there is a definitive ruling on the operating conditions of the sector.”

With the partnership interrupted, the club estimates a loss of R$90 million for 2027.

Last Monday (16th), Flamengo’s board submitted its budget proposal for the upcoming season to the Board of Directors, with projections pointing to significant changes in the club’s financial planning.

Among the points presented are the suspension of the master sponsorship and the expectation that construction of the Gasômetro Stadium is unlikely to happen in the near future.

On the pitch, meanwhile, Flamengo leads the Brazilian Championship and faces Athletico-PR this Wednesday (18th).

“Betano announces the suspension of its sponsorship of Flamengo given the continued uncertainty surrounding the fixed-odds betting sector and the lack of a definitive ruling on Provisional Measure 1,394/2026.

Since the measure was published on September 25, the company has been adapting its operations to the new reality imposed on the legal and regulated market, focusing on preserving jobs and maintaining its commitments to social projects and to the Club.

Even though it was unable to display its brand on the uniforms or commercially use the assets provided for in the agreement, Betano sought to preserve the sponsorship for as long as possible, recognizing the importance of this investment for football, for Olympic sports, and for the professionals involved in these activities.

The prolongation of this scenario, however, led the company to decide to suspend the sponsorship until there is a definitive ruling on the operating conditions of the sector.

Betano reaffirms its respect for Flamengo, its athletes, staff, and fans, and remains committed to Brazil and to building a responsible, regulated, and safe market.”

title: The 51% Club names HSBC UK as its regional banking partner
article_text:
The 51% Club, a national network for female founders and leaders, has named HSBC UK as its Regional Banking Partner, giving its community of more than 2,500 women closer access to the bank’s support for women-led businesses.

The two organisations said the partnership is intended to open up opportunities for women in business and to make the Midlands one of the best places in the UK for women-led enterprise to grow and scale. It will run across The 51% Club’s events and programmes, with further activity to be announced in the coming months.

The 51% Club was founded in Birmingham and now operates from five hubs nationally: Birmingham, Leamington Spa, Leicester, London and Worcester, with more launching. It has grown over just over two years and is organised around four “rooms”, Grow, Scale, Exit and Lead, which cover stages from building a first business to scaling, selling and leading at the top of an organisation.

Alongside a calendar of monthly events and programmes, the network runs an annual conference, IGNITE, which welcomed 250 founders to Millennium Point in Birmingham in September.

Under the agreement, members will gain closer access to HSBC UK’s Women’s Business Growth Initiative, which offers events, networking, masterclasses and personalised funding support to women business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs. According to the bank, funding conversations are handled by a Business Specialist for borrowing up to £100k and by a Relationship Manager above that, with lending subject to status.

The bank first launched the initiative as a £250m funding programme in September 2024.

Members will also be able to use the HSBC Small Business Growth Programme, which is free and open to all businesses and offers insights, events and short training sessions.

Both organisations pointed to figures showing that only two to four per cent of women-led businesses in the UK reach £1m in revenue, and said they see the partnership as a way to change those numbers in the region and beyond.

Tara Attfield-Tomes, founder of The 51% Club, said: “We are so proud to welcome HSBC UK as our Regional Banking Partner. From the very beginning, The 51% Club has been about building a real ecosystem for women in business, providing the support, the rooms, and the relationships they deserve, and doing it properly.”

She added: “HSBC UK’s commitment to women entrepreneurs through its Women’s Business Growth Initiative sits right alongside that mission, so this is a partnership that just makes sense. For our community, it means even closer access to real support as they grow, and I can’t wait to see what we build together.”

Jagdeep Rai, managing director and UK head of coverage, SME business banking, at HSBC UK, said: “I’m proud to partner with The 51% Club to bring our community of women business owners together and support them throughout their business journey. Through education, meaningful connections and networking, alongside personalised one-to-one funding conversations, we can help open the door to new possibilities and give women the confidence and support to take their businesses forward.”

Tom Wood, head of SME business banking at HSBC UK, cited the share of venture capital reaching all-female founding teams. “HSBC UK is committed to removing barriers that prevent women founders from starting, sustaining and scaling businesses. With female-only businesses receiving just 2% of venture capital in 2024, initiatives such as our Women’s Business Growth Initiative and our new partnership with The 51% Club are vital,” he said.

He added: “We also have our Small Business Growth programme which provides training, networking and events to help founders navigate funding and build resilience. Together, we can unlock more opportunities for women-led businesses and strengthen the UK economy.”

The announcement follows other recent efforts to widen support for female entrepreneurs, including a Built By Her crowdfunding campaign that raised £100k for women-led businesses last year.

Founders looking for recognition can also enter the Business Matters Female Founders Awards. The awards are open to female founders and co-founders of independent UK businesses that have traded for at least two years. Entries close at 23:59 on 12 March 2027, and the list will be published on 14 May 2027.

title: Tour de France widens sponsorship gap over Giro and Vuelta, says GlobalData
article_text:
The Tour de France has cemented its commercial dominance over cycling’s other two Grand Tours in 2026, leading on sponsorship value, media reach and prize money, according to GlobalData.

The firm’s report, “Post-Event Analysis – Cycling Grand Tours 2026”, found that the Giro d’Italia signed the highest number of partners and the Vuelta a España leaned on its shared organiser ASO, but neither matched the Tour’s long-term commercial power.

Value at the Tour is concentrated among a small group of jersey and main partners. LCL, E.Leclerc, Skoda, Krys, Continental and Groupama together account for more than half of the race’s sponsorship value.

Olivia Snooks, sport analyst at GlobalData, said: “The Tour de France remains cycling’s most valuable property by some distance. Its jersey sponsors are mostly French brands buying national visibility, and media contracts running to 2030 give ASO a secure revenue base. Even with live UK coverage moving behind a paywall for the first time in four decades, TNT Sports reported strong audience growth, which shows how much demand the race commands.”

The Tour also has the broadest media footprint of the three races. Free-to-air television remains the backbone of both the Tour and the Vuelta, reflecting ASO’s preference for public service broadcasters that maximise reach for sponsors. As ASO organises the Tour and co-organises the Vuelta, the two races share most of their broadcasters, with most media deals secured to the end of the decade.

The Giro, organised by RCS Sport, sells its rights separately and relies more on pay-TV. It has confirmed long-term terms for only one of its media deals, with Warner Bros. Discovery.

Snooks said: “The Giro sells volume and destinations. It has the largest sponsor roster of the three races, but regional governments and tourism bodies, from Friuli Venezia Giulia to Abruzzo and Valle d’Aosta, fund almost a third of its sponsorship value as they pay to host stages and promote themselves.

“The Bulgarian Grande Partenza delivered record audiences for Eurosport and HBO Max, but since Enel’s long-running deal ended, the maglia rosa has relied on stopgap sponsors. Securing a long-term anchor partner remains the Giro’s main commercial gap.”

The Vuelta has the smallest sponsorship portfolio of the three and no dominant partner. Title sponsor Carrefour leads a roster built mostly on modest deals with Spanish brands.

Prize money follows the same hierarchy: Tadej Pogačar’s winner’s prize at the Tour was nearly double what Jonas Vingegaard earned for winning the Giro, and more than three times Enric Mas’ prize for winning the Vuelta.

Snooks added: “Pogačar and Vingegaard shaped the 2026 season. One won the Giro, the other the Tour, and both crashed out of another Grand Tour. The drop in online engagement at the Vuelta after Pogačar’s exit shows both the value and the risk of relying on a few headline names. For the Vuelta, larger stand-alone Spanish and international partnerships would help narrow the gap with its two bigger rivals, rather than relying on agreements shared with the Tour.”

title: Disney+ bolsters ESPN portfolio in Spain with WOW FC MMA rights
article_text:
US media giant Disney’s Disney+ OTT streaming service has expanded its sports rights portfolio in Spain, adding domestic mixed martial arts (MMA) promotion Way of Warriors FC (WOW FC).

Through the ‘exclusive’ domestic right agreement, Disney+ will broadcast live WOW FC fight nights live and on demand, alongside ancillary content and shoulder programming, on the ESPN-branded content area of its platform, at no extra cost to subscribers.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

This deal will begin with the upcoming WOW 34 event at Valencia’s 15,600-capacity Roig Arena on November 21.

Speaking on the announcement, Disney+ country manager for Spain Simon Anselm said: “The arrival of WOW FC on ESPN on Disney+ reinforces our commitment to offering our customers new forms of entertainment.

“MMA combines competition, excitement and spectacle, and this agreement allows us to bring the experience of its live fight nights to a broader audience, while also bringing them closer to the stories behind its fighters.”

Ilia Topuria, a two-time champion in the major UFC promotion and a partner in WOW FC, added: “Disney+, through ESPN, has played a major role in the growth and global expansion of MMA, helping to turn our sport into a global phenomenon.

“This agreement represents much more than a distribution agreement: it is a historic step for MMA in Spain and an extraordinary opportunity for our athletes to inspire millions of people. I am convinced that together we are going to build something truly special.”

This follows the recent launch of ESPN as a content area on Disney+ to select markets across Europe, positioning the sports broadcasting brand as Disney’s key consumer sports arm.

In Spain in particular, the platform holds the rights to UEFA Women's Champions League soccer, Formula E motor racing, NHL ice hockey, and more.

The wider lineup also features college sports such as the NCAA men's and women's basketball tournaments (March Madness), college football playoffs, and bowl games, as well as other sports rights in select markets, most recent of those being the NHL, and NBA basketball in 11 European markets, including neighboring Portugal.

title: Scottish Rugby extends two partnership agreements
article_text:
Saltire Energy has agreed a three-year extension to a relationship that began in 2021. The Aberdeen-based company will continue to support Scotland Men’s international matchdays alongside two grassroots programmes, the Saltire Energy Rugby Schools Week and Saltire Energy Caledonia Cup.

The Schools Week programme has engaged more than 70,000 pupils at over 600 state schools since its launch in 2021 and forms part of Scottish Rugby’s State School Strategy. The Saltire Energy Caledonia Cup also brought together more than 600 young players for its regional Finals Day in March.

Alongside that agreement, Highland Spring has extended its exclusive relationship with Scottish Rugby for a further two years and will remain Official Water Supplier until at least 2028.

Since the partnership began in 2024, Highland Spring has supplied more than 90,000 litres of water to Scotland’s men’s, women’s and U20 teams, as well as Glasgow Warriors and Edinburgh Rugby.

The next phase of the partnership will include increased on-field visibility, further content around hydration and a coaching session or community day at a local rugby club involving a former Scotland player. Highland Spring products will also remain available at Scottish Gas Murrayfield, alongside a recycling programme for empty bottles.

The partnership generated 5.4 million social and digital impressions across its first two seasons, according to Scottish Rugby, while television exposure reached 9.56 million during 2025/26.

Together, the two renewals extend support across both elite and grassroots rugby in Scotland. While Saltire Energy will continue its involvement with international matchdays and youth participation, Highland Spring will retain a role spanning Scotland’s national teams, professional clubs, supporters and community activity

Simon Oldham, Managing Director of Highland SpringGroup, said, “Highland Spring and Scottish Rugby are two Scottish icons, perfectly matched through shared values and a passion for helping people perform at their best. Over the past two years, we’ve built an authentic and highly collaborative relationship – and this extension marks a bold next chapter

“Healthy hydration is essential to performance on and off the pitch. Our increased investment will help us take that message to even more people while continuing to hydrate Scotland’s players and supporters.”

Olaf Gueldner, Chief Customer Officer at Scottish Rugby, said, “The commitment from Saltire Energy to Scottish Rugby over the duration of the partnership is testament to the many shared values between our organisations. We are both passionate about supporting the game at grassroots level through our community clubs and schools.

Mike Loggie, CEO of Saltire Energy, said, “Saltire Energy is proud to continue our official partnership with Scottish Rugby. As we celebrate our 40th year in business, our partnership with SRU reinforces our commitment to the communities we operate in and our dedication to the role sport plays in young people’s lives.”

title: Fit-again Quewin Nortje eyes Dubai and Cape Town return as Blitzboks launch SVNS defence
article_text:
After spending nearly six months on the sidelines, fit-again flyer Quewin Nortje is determined to make up for lost time when the Springbok Sevens launch their HSBC SVNS title defence in Dubai next weekend.

While the 23-year-old wing recovered in time to help the Blitzboks claim back-to-back World Championship crowns across Hong Kong, Valladolid, and Bordeaux earlier this year, a stubborn hamstring injury forced him to miss all six legs of the 2026 regular series.

Now boasting a full, uninterrupted pre-season at the squad's Stellenbosch training base, Nortje has his sights firmly set on making the final 13-man cut – named tomorrow – for both Dubai and the following weekend's home tournament in Cape Town.

“I know selection is not guaranteed for any tournament, and coach Philip Snyman explained to us that he is also looking at building squad depth, but I am very keen to make it into the Dubai and Cape Town squads having missed out the last time around,” Nortje said.

“We won in Dubai in 2024 when I made my debut, so it will always be special, while playing in Cape Town remains the biggest highlight for any Blitzbok. To play in front of your family, friends, and those who made sacrifices for you to live your dream remains a very special feeling.”

Boasting an impressive strike rate of 36 tries (180 points) across 15 tournaments, Nortje’s return provides significant firepower for a Blitzbok side chasing a third consecutive Cape Town title. His comeback could also feature a nostalgic reunion: former Afrikaanse Hoër Seunskool (Affies) track teammate Van Reenen Kruger is among the trimmed 16-man group vying for Dubai selection.

“We were in the same year group and ran track together at Affies in Pretoria, and in fact, we were part of the relay team that broke a longstanding record,” Nortje recalled. “Van Reenen is a very capable sevens player as well. I watched him play this season at the Safari Sevens and he was great. On the track I always handed the baton over to him for the next leg; imagine I could pass him the ball for his first try.”

Nortje’s hunger reflects a broader competitive edge in Stellenbosch. While Snyman has retained the vast majority of the squad that secured the 2026 SVNS Series and World Championship double – losing only Mfundo Ndhlovu and Donavan Don to Vodacom United Rugby Championship commitments – the coach is deliberately expanding his player pool.

With qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games hinging on final placings at the 2027 World Championship events, Snyman will use the opening six series tournaments to test emerging talent alongside his established core.

South Africa will open their campaign without four regulars, as Impi Visser, Zander Reynders, Jayden Nell, and Shilton van Wyk are still in rehabilitation and have been ruled out of the opening leg.

“Most of our established group of players are fit and ready, apart from the four injured players, while we also invited some very exciting younger talents into camp,” Snyman explained, noting the inclusion of Junior Springboks, Varsity Cup standouts, and franchise loan signings like Stormers back JC Mars.

“No one in the contracted group is resting on their laurels, while the new players are pushing hard for more permanent opportunities, and that delivers a very competitive environment.”

The Blitzboks will travel to the Middle East on Monday next week, ahead of the season opener at The Sevens Stadium on 28 and 29 November. Alongside the main touring party, Snyman will take a second, younger group to compete in the Dubai International Invitational Tournament to gain vital exposure against international opposition.

title: Silverstone launches UK charity foundation
article_text:
The Foundation will begin operating across Silverstone events from 2027, consolidating fundraising activity under one organisation. It builds on charitable work associated with CarFest, the festival founded by Chris Evans, which moved to Silverstone in 2026.

The launch follows a year in which Silverstone raised more than £1 million for children’s charities. A significant proportion was generated through CarFest, with further support coming through the Formula 1 British Grand Prix for organisations including Starlight Children’s Foundation, Roald Dahl’s Marvellous Children’s Charity and Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity.

From 2027, fundraising opportunities will extend across Silverstone’s calendar, providing motorsport spectators and other visitors with opportunities to contribute. The Foundation’s trustees will select charities to receive funding each year, with a combination of national and local organisations supported.

The first national charities selected for 2027 include BBC Children in Need, Ellen MacArthur Cancer Trust, Rainbow Trust Children’s Charity, Spinal Track, Starlight Children’s Foundation, Teenage Cancer Trust and Young Epilepsy. Further organisations, including local community causes, are due to be added during the year.

The initiative has particular relevance within British motorsport because Silverstone hosts the Formula 1 British Grand Prix alongside a wider programme of national and international racing. Fundraising connected to the circuit’s major events will now sit within the Foundation’s wider structure from 2027.

The Silverstone Foundation forms part of the circuit’s wider environmental, social and governance activity and creates a single framework for charitable fundraising involving spectators, partners and staff across its annual events programme.

Darren Beddard, Chair of the Trustees and Chief Financial Officer at Silverstone, said, “Selecting this year’s charities was an incredibly difficult task, as every applicant makes a significant contribution to the lives of children in the UK. By channelling the generosity of Silverstone’s fans, partners and staff through one Foundation, we can be more effective and make a real difference to many more young lives.”

title: Campari Group makes football sponsorship debut with Aperol-UEFA EURO 2028 partnership
article_text:
Campari Group is entering the international football sponsorship landscape through a landmark partnership between its Aperol brand and UEFA, becoming the official spritz partner of UEFA EURO 2028 and the European Qualifiers.

The agreement marks Campari Group’s first-ever partnership with UEFA and its first major international football sponsorship. The collaboration provides Aperol with a platform to strengthen its global brand presence by associating with one of European football’s premier sporting events.

The partnership will extend across the European Qualifiers and the UEFA EURO 2028 final tournament, giving Aperol visibility throughout the competition cycle. The tournament will be hosted across England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland, with 24 national teams competing in 51 matches.

As part of the agreement, Aperol will develop consumer engagement initiatives and brand activations around the competition, centred on shared celebrations and social experiences. The association also reflects the brand’s Italian aperitivo heritage and its positioning around bringing people together.

Simon Hunt, CEO of Campari Group, said, “This partnership brings to life our purpose of unlocking human connections on a global stage that unites millions of fans. As our first major international football partnership and first-ever sponsorship with UEFA, UEFA EURO 2028 gives Aperol an exceptional opportunity to engage audiences at scale and support the brand’s ambition to expand its presence across our new formats and opening up new occasions.”

Guy-Laurent Epstein, UEFA Executive Director of Marketing, added, “We are delighted to partner with Campari Group and welcome their iconic brand Aperol as an official sponsor of UEFA EURO 2028 and the European Qualifiers. UEFA EURO is much more than a football tournament; it is a celebration that brings people together through unforgettable shared experiences. Aperol’s longstanding ability to create moments of connection and conviviality makes it a natural fit for our events, and we look forward to working together to create a memorable tournament.”

The agreement comes as Campari Group looks to accelerate Aperol’s international expansion. The company highlighted the brand’s growth from approximately 60 million Aperol Spritz servings annually two decades ago to around 1.5 billion today. It is also extending the brand’s portfolio through formats such as Aperol Spritz On Tap, Ready to Serve and Ready to Drink.

For Campari Group, the UEFA partnership represents an opportunity to leverage football’s international reach to broaden consumer engagement and create new occasions for brand consumption.

title: Iran war dents Middle East sports model as events are canceled or postponed. F1 bucks the trend
article_text:
Two season-ending Formula 1 races in the Middle East are going ahead despite the war in Iran and retaliatory attacks across the region that have canceled or postponed other large sports events. This includes two Formula 1 races earlier this year in Saudi Arabia and Bahrain.

The conflict has upended the region's image as a safe haven where governments and sponsors have kicked in billions to lure mega-sports events. This comes as Europe and North America appear wary of such lavish spending.

“The situation could change but the geography will not change,” Sebastian Sons, who follows sports in the Middle East with the German research institute CARPO, told The Associated Press. “The Middle East and the Gulf region are always a volatile and fragile region.”

Going ahead is an endorsement for doing business in the region, but has also prompted concerns about safety from some teams and staff. Mohammed Ben Sulayem, the president of auto racing's world governing body FIA, has said “we are fully prepared” to pull off the two races: Qatar on Nov. 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6.

Ben Sulayem is from the United Arab Emirates.

A MotoGP race was held in Qatar on Nov. 8 on the track where F1 races. MotoGP is operated by Liberty Media, which also runs F1.

“Holding the races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi signals that those two are stable and able to host large-scale sporting events. It is important they are seen to be open for business,” Kristian Ulrichsen, a political scientist at Rice University's Baker Institute, told The AP.

“Predictability in long-term decision-making and policy planning,” Ulrichsen added, “made the region so attractive as a host of mega-events at a time when many cities and countries around the world are rethinking the cost of doing so.”

Qatar’s reputation is on the line. It held the 2022 World Cup and is a co-favorite — with India — to land the 2036 Olympics. It’s also host next year to the basketball World Cup (Aug. 27-Sept. 12) and has the 2030 Asian Games.

It took a hit last week when the United States pulled its team from the boys’ under-17 World Cup being played in Qatar.

Saudi Arabia and its Persian Gulf neighbors have spent big to hold major sports events but were cutting back on mega-sports funding before the war began nine months ago.

“For Saudi, the war has accelerated the need to find economies, to maybe reassess what was feasible and what wasn’t,” Ulrichsen said. He said landing the “big prize,” two years ago — the 2034 World Cup — probably honed Saudi's focus.

“Qatar and the UAE will probably have to at some point do the same,” he added.

Major events called off, postponed or relocated include the two Formula 1 races earlier in the season, and the WTA season-ending tennis finals and soccer’s monthlong Asian Cup — both originally scheduled for Saudi Arabia. The 2027 Dakar Rally was also moved from Saudi Arabia to Portugal and Morocco.

The region has been using sports to promote “soft power” to enhance its brand. But Saudi Arabia now faces hard power with Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels having struck Saudi Arabia’s main international airport in Riyadh. Riyadh’s business district has also recently been targeted.

The war has also affected the large Gulf air carriers and changed travel patterns in the region.

“One of the things Iran did during the war was to deliberately attack the connective tissue between Gulf states and the world,” Sascha Bruchmann, an analyst at the International Institute for Strategic Studies, told The AP. “This includes ports, airports, hotels and data centers — signaling that Iran can attack important issues beyond hydrocarbons and challenge the Gulf states’ ambitions to diversify.”

Sons, the researcher at the German think tank, estimated that Saudi Arabia invested more than $6 billion in international sports between 2021 and 2023. Sons said the country hosted more than 100 international sports events between 2019 and 2024.

A visible failure was the bankruptcy of LIV Golf, which reports say was funded by approximately $5 billion from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund. Saudi Arabia also canceled the 2029 Asian Winter Games, planned for the Trojena ski village in the south of the desert kingdom.

The event has been moved to Almaty, Kazakhstan, which lost to Beijing in a close vote for the 2022 Winter Olympics.

Ulrichsen said Saudi Arabia was backing off what seemed like a “scattergun approach,” backing LIV Golf, planning an unlikely Winter Asian Games, bankrolling soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo, and buying the Premier League team Newcastle. All are varied approaches to “soft power.”

Ronaldo is reported to earn more than $200 million annually with Saudi club Al-Nassr.

Qatar's sovereign wealth fund controls French club Paris Saint-Germain, and Manchester City is controlled by an Abu Dhabi investment group. Ulrichsen argued sports teams are a more effective investment than World Cups or Olympics “because people care more about the teams they support than an event that happens for three or four weeks.”

“When Ronaldo would post on Instagram about the amazing lifestyle he was enjoying in Riyadh, that would reach upward of a half a billion people,” Ulrichsen added. “You simply can't buy that kind of reach with a conventional PR campaign.”

title: FOX, NBC, get two of ex-ESPN games at center of NFL media rights talks
article_text:
The NFL is indeed set for additional broadcast television inventory this coming season, with FOX and NBC receiving some of the ex-ESPN inventory that at one point was earmarked for YouTube.

The NFL awarded FOX and NBC one game each out of the four windows ESPN relinquished as part of its deal to acquire NFL Network, Sports Media Watch has learned. The league is also expected to convert one regionally distributed game each on FOX and CBS to a national window.

The end result will be four additional national windows on broadcast television using a mix of new and existing inventory.

The league had been expected to see a slight increase in broadcast television inventory this season, and the ex-ESPN windows will functionally shift cable-exclusive inventory to broadcast. (Officially, the four ex-ESPN windows contractually belonged to ABC and ESPN+ as part of overlapping “Monday Night Football” doubleheaders. But with ABC apparently set to simulcast ESPN games in those four weeks instead, the change amounts to dropping four ESPN-exclusive editions of “MNF.”)

Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch said on an earnings call Monday that the company’s new windows would consist of a Week 10 International Series game from Munich, which would air in an early morning window as part of a FOX tripleheader — the first NFL tripleheader on a single broadcast network since 2016. The second would be a Saturday game in Week 15. It was not clear which game came out of the ex-ESPN inventory and which was elevated from the Fox regional slate.

NBC announced Monday that its additional inventory would be a Saturday game in Week 17 leading into its annual Peacock-exclusive game, giving the company three exclusive windows that week.

CBS announced later Monday that its additional game window will air on primetime on the Saturday of Week 15, creating a split-network doubleheader with Fox on December 19. That is likely to be the day on which the College Football Playoff schedules the bulk of its first round games.

The additional broadcast TV inventory comes as the NFL faces a federal investigation into its rights deals with streaming companies that has been cheerled — and potentially may have even been sparked — by Fox Corporation.

The four ex-ESPN windows were originally expected to form the bulk of a new five-game media rights package — also including the league’s new International Series game from Australia — that the league had been reportedly shopping throughout the offseason. At some point in the process, the NFL is said to have shifted from shopping a single five-game package to splitting that inventory between Netflix and Google-owned YouTube. John Ourand of Puck reported last week that YouTube was not interested in that arrangement, and the two games it would have received were instead shopped to broadcast television.

The other two games are expected to go to Netflix, which would presumably form a ‘five-game package’ featuring those two contests, the Australia game, and its existing Christmas Day inventory.

title: NFL reportedly wants new rights deals in place by start of next season
article_text:
The timeline is accelerating for the NFL’s expedited media rights negotiations.

John Ourand of Puck reported Thursday that the NFL is now believed to want its new media rights deals completed before the new season begins in September, earlier than the fall timeframe that had been previously reported. The league is expected to negotiate and announce its new deals one-by-one, starting with Paramount and then Fox, Ourand wrote, with all of them taking effect immediately.

Technically, the NFL does not have the ability to exit its current media rights deals until after the 2029 season at the earliest (2030 for ESPN), but there is little expectation that any of the league’s partners will oppose the expedited talks. According to Ourand, it is believed that the new contracts will run through the 2033 or 2034 seasons, meaning that the existing rightsholders can lock up NFL rights for the next seven or eight years by agreeing to the early talks. Currently, the networks are guaranteed only four additional seasons if they choose to wait for the league’s contractual opt-out.

But the early talks are likely to come with some sacrifices, and not just the obvious financial ones. The NFL is expected to use the opening created by the negotiations to carve out inventory for new packages. NFL EVP/media distribution Hans Schroeder told Alex Sherman of CNBC last month that the league plans to engage not just its existing partners in its upcoming talks, but additional suitors who are on the outside looking in. Schroeder: “We’re going to listen and probably have a lot of different people that want to have that want to have a conversation with us.”

The league is already believed to be shopping the four game windows that were freed up as part of its now-completed sale of NFL Network to ESPN, with Austin Karp and Ben Fischer of Sports Business Journal reporting last week that YouTube is among the frontrunners for that package.

The incumbent rights partners are likely to end up in the position of paying more for less, but given the ability to guarantee that they will remain in the NFL business into the middle of the next decade, it is unlikely that any will turn up their nose at the chance.

title: Analyst predicts Walmart as surprise buyer for sports media rights in 2027
article_text:
The sports media rights marketplace is preparing for a shakeup.

As the decade nears its end and the NFL almost certainly exits its current set of media rights deals, networks and streamers are preparing for what could be a monumental shift in the industry. Legacy broadcasters continue to consolidate or get spun off from their corporate parents, while streaming giants continue to battle each other for engagement. The NFL is the 3,000-pound gorilla in the room that will dictate how networks and streamers approach other media rights opportunities in the next several years.

Major properties that will be on the market before or during NFL negotiations include the 2030 FIFA World Cup (set to be awarded by the end of 2026), MLB, NHL, and Premier League (all of which expire in 2028), Big Ten and PGA Tour (2030), and NASCAR (2031).

The usual suspects will kick the tires on some or all of these. ESPN, Skydance (CBS/TNT), Fox, NBC/Peacock, Prime Video, Netflix, Apple, YouTube, Versant, The CW, Ion, and DAZN will all be in the mix. But one company that might come out of left field is Walmart, according to Bank of America Securities analyst Jessica Reif Ehrlich, who floated the retailer as a potential bidder for live sports in 2027.

Ehrlich revealed her prediction at a Sports Business Journal conference on Tuesday, which reportedly drew “intrigued murmurs from the audience.”

Walmart would be an unconventional bidder, to say the least. It does not own a major streaming service, nor any broadcast or cable networks. Walmart does, however, own Vizio, a television brand it acquired for $2.3 billion in December 2024. Since the acquisition, Vizio has risen to the third most popular television brand in America, behind Samsung and LG.

Walmart’s acquisition focused on scaling its advertising and media businesses. Each Vizio television set comes preloaded with its own smart TV interface and the WatchFree+ app, a Vizio-owned FAST platform that features over 400 live and local channels and a vast library of movies and shows.

Should Walmart enter the sports-rights market, its strategy could be similar to Roku’s, which is seen as one of Vizio’s primary competitors in the space. Roku has acquired some smaller, more affordable packages like Sunday morning MLB games (2024-2025) users onto its FAST platform, The Roku Channel.

It seems unlikely that Walmart would get in the mix for a major rights package, though the company is certainly capitalized enough to do so if it wanted.

title: Aussie Broadband Renews Western Sydney Wanderers FC Partnership for 2026/27 A-League Season
article_text:
Australian telecommunications provider Aussie Broadband has extended its partnership with the Western Sydney Wanderers FC for the 2026/27 season. Building upon a successful two-year commercial partnership, the renewal confirms Aussie Broadband will continue as the club’s Official Telecommunications Partner, Official Grassroots Football Partner, and Senior Partner. The agreement reinforces corporate investment across both elite match-day operations at CommBank Stadium and regional community engagement across Western Sydney.

Under the renewed terms, Aussie Broadband maintains naming and supporting rights across key community and volunteer properties, including the Wander Crew match-day volunteer programme, the Club Ambassador Program, and the Community Champions initiative. A central activation pillar of the agreement remains the annual Grassroots Recognition Round, which spotlights local clubs, administrators, and volunteers driving football participation growth throughout Western Sydney.

Aussie Broadband group chief financial officer, Darren Rowland, emphasised the alignment between the telecommunications operator’s local-first business model and the Wanderers’ regional community footprint.

“We’re thrilled to continue our partnership with Western Sydney Wanderers FC for this year’s A-League season.

“Aussie Broadband was built on a commitment to supporting local communities, and that remains a core part of who we are today.

“The Wanderers share that same community-first mindset, making this a natural partnership.

“We hope our support helps the club build on their positive impact across Western Sydney, bringing people together and strengthening connections throughout the community,” Rowland said.

Western Sydney Wanderers CEO, Scott Hudson, highlighted the commercial and social value of partnering with an organisation invested in volunteer and grassroots recognition.

“We’re incredibly proud to be continuing our partnership with Aussie Broadband, an organisation that genuinely understands the value of community and the importance of supporting the people who make football what it is.”

“From our Wander Crew volunteers who give so much of their time on match days, to the grassroots clubs and individuals working tirelessly to grow the game across Western Sydney, this partnership is about recognising the people who are so often the unsung heroes of our sport.

“What has made this relationship so meaningful is Aussie Broadband’s willingness to invest in initiatives that create genuine connections and make a positive difference beyond the football pitch.

“We’re delighted to have their continued support for the 2026/27 season and look forward to building on the foundations we’ve established together,” Hudson said.

title: Anytime Fitness Australia Named Official Gym Partner of West Coast Eagles
article_text:
Anytime Fitness Australia has signed a two-year commercial agreement to become the Official Gym Partner of the West Coast Eagles, spanning both the club’s Australian Football League (AFL) and AFL Women’s (AFLW) programmes.

The partnership connects the national fitness franchise network, comprising more than 647 clubs and 800,000 members nationwide, directly with the Eagles’ record-breaking supporter base of 115,324 financial members across Western Australia.

By linking Anytime Fitness’s club footprint across Greater Perth, the Peel region, and regional Western Australia with the Eagles’ elite men’s and women’s squads, the deal aims to bridge high-performance sport with everyday community health.

The agreement follows Anytime Fitness’s recent major activation in Perth as the Official Gym Partner of ExPRO, Australia’s fitness, wellness, and lifestyle festival, further consolidating the brand’s commercial and recruitment expansion along the Western Australian coastline.

Anytime Fitness Australia Managing Director, Simon Thompson, highlighted the value of aligning with Western Australia’s largest sporting institution to drive grassroots fitness participation.

“The West Coast Eagles unite generations of West Australians, with a loyalty and pride that reaches far beyond the football field.”

“Our ambition is to give more people across WA a welcoming place to train, build strength and feel their best.

“Becoming the Official Gym Partner of the Eagles’ AFL and AFLW teams builds on that commitment, bringing together two organisations that share a passion for sport, fitness and the positive role they play in people’s lives,” Thompson said.

West Coast Eagles CEO, Don Pyke, underscored the natural synergy between elite athletic performance and accessible community wellbeing.

“We’re proud to welcome Anytime Fitness to the West Coast Eagles and look forward to building a strong partnership across our AFL and AFLW programs.”

“Both organisations understand the important role sport and physical activity can play in bringing people together and supporting their health and wellbeing.

“We’re excited to work together to encourage more people in our community to get active and enjoy the benefits of an active lifestyle,” Pyke said.
