Replacements: Ryan Elias, Gareth Thomas, Dillon Lewis, Taine Plumtree, Kane James, Reuben Morgan-Williams, Joe Hawkins, Louie Hennessey.

Replacements: Billy Pollard, Angus Bell, Allan Alaalatoa, Jeremy Williams, Fraser McReight, Kalani Thomas, Ben Donaldson, Filipo Daugunu.

title: PWR: RFU wants to 'protect Red Roses' with reduction in international players
article_text:
World rugby has endured a few shocks and upsets in 2026 - and England's women losing back-to-back Test matches to Canada was among the biggest.

But with 25 Canadians plying their trade on English soil in Premiership Women's Rugby (PWR) last season, their success on the international stage comes at a time when PWR has been in discussions with the Rugby Football Union (RFU) to review the numbers of overseas players in the league.

"We are keen to attract star talent into PWR to continue to make it the best league in the world," said RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney.

"But we've also got to protect England Red Roses' interests as well."

Changes have been planned for the 2027-28 PWR season around injury dispensation for foreign players, with the removal of club injury credit which helps to cover the cost of replacing an injured player.

Only players who sustain an injury while on international duty for one of England's representative teams will be eligible.

However, discussions have gone further around the numbers of English Qualified Players (EQP) required in matchday squads.

Speaking to BBC Sport, Sweeney said: "We're talking about it. Currently, there's 13 EQP in PWR. It's 15 in the [men's] Prem.

"We're always concerned about the amount of game time that's occurring for under-23 players coming through the system. Are they getting enough game time?

"We're having conversations with PWR in terms of how we can maximise that, so it is a live topic."

England had been on a 41-match unbeaten streak - dating back almost four years - before twice losing to Canada in the WXV Global Series last month.

It prompted a warning from head coach John Mitchell that too many overseas players in the PWR could be detrimental for future Red Roses sides.

The league has increasingly attracted the best global talent. In recent years, a majority of Scotland and Wales players have played in PWR and since the 2025 World Cup, more players have joined from New Zealand.

The highest-profile arrival last season was Black Ferns captain Ruahei Demant linking up with Bristol, while Ruby Tui has joined Trailfinders Women for the new campaign.

And while many neutrals believe Canada's growing success is good for the women's game, Sweeney says England must keep "raising the bar".

"It doesn't feel it's good for the game for us, we never want to lose - but it had to come at some stage," he said.

"Seeing the growth in the Canadian team, largely due to where they play in PWR - it's encouraging that the standards are rising.

"We're conscious that unions like Ireland are investing much more heavily now into the women's game as well, so it is good for the game.

"From our perspective, we just want to keep raising the bar and challenging people to catch us and challenge us."

Canada and Saracens scrum-half Olivia Apps was named PWR player of the season when her club lifted the 2025-26 trophy.

She says exposure to the PWR has massively benefited Canadian rugby.

"It's the best women's league right now to play in and the best quality competition," she told BBC Sport.

"We don't have a league back home, so to be able to come from the universities and play with and against the best players in the world is going to make us better for sure."

Asked if she was worried Canadian players would not get as much game time in the future, Apps said: "I would hope not. I think that would diminish the quality of the PWR.

"Internationals make this league what it is, and credit to the English players, but the internationals really do contribute in a great way.

"Any coach or team that has a Canadian on their side loves to have that Canadian because they work hard, they bring the physicality, the athleticism and a great style of rugby."

Reducing foreign imports would allow young English talent more PWR game time, but the move does not come without concerns.

"The league itself is to create Red Roses and to create English players for the future. If we are going to bring non-EQP players into the league, then they have to add to the league, so they have to be of a world-class standard," said Loughborough Lightning head coach Nathan Smith.

But Smith does envisage a problem if the league changes before investing in the pathways.

"There's a pinch point at the start of next season where we'll have Lions, England camp and a Premiership Cup. My simple question is, are there enough players to fulfil all three?" he said.

"England Under-20s and Under-18s aren't performing on the world stage, therefore what can we do to support that? We need a level of competition that sits below the PWR that fulfils their needs for development."

A PWR spokesperson said: "There is no difference of opinion between us and the RFU on this and developing the next generation of Red Roses is a specific, stated objective of the PWR.

"We will continue to work collaboratively with the RFU on EQP and any other matter which is important to the future of women's rugby in this country."

The new PWR season starts on Friday as Loughborough Lightning host Trailfinders.

For now, overseas stars will remain a key part of the league's success, but how many are allowed to feature in the future may define its next chapter.

title: Tamaiti Williams reaches major milestone in recovery from disc-eating infection
article_text:
Tamaiti Williams has reached a significant milestone in his recovery from the back infection that ended his 2026 season after just two games for the Crusaders: running.

The All Blacks prop has been sidelined since discovering that methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) had been eating a disc in his lower back, causing immense pain and putting more than just his rugby career in jeopardy.

Following a surgical procedure that included fusing two discs together, Williams has been slowly progressing through a lengthy rehab process as he eyes an eventual return to rugby.

The 26-year-old was named in the Crusaders’ 2027 squad, but with an injury replacement in Frenchman Clément Castets, signalling he is expected to miss at least part of the coming season.

One month later, Williams’ timeline remains uncertain, but the club shared a promising update to their social media channels on Thursday afternoon. The 27-Test All Black was shown jogging on a treadmill while attached to a load-sharing machine, which was holding 25 per cent of his body weight to ease the stress on his lower body and back.

“I feel fit. I feel light,” he said, grinning in the video. “It feels pretty foreign, though. I haven’t run since March, before all of the chaos happened. It feels good, though. No pain, which is good.”

Williams said his body “feels good” after his first run in eight months, adding: “We’ll get our recovery done and then we’ll go again.”

Crusaders physio John Roche was by Williams’ side for the milestone, and was thrilled to see it all go smoothly.

“This piece of kit is pretty amazing; it weighs the athlete, and then we can adjust the percentage of body weight so they can run at less than their full body weight. So, Tams is running at 75 per cent of his body weight at the moment.

“The treadmill can go up to 30 kilometres an hour, so you can run fast, but obviously he’s not going to do that for his first run. It’s just great to see the big man up and running.”

title: All Blacks to address mentality concerns ahead of decisive England Test
article_text:
All Blacks forwards coach Jason Ryan emerged from Saturday’s historic loss to Wales with questions over his team’s mentality in the match, questions he intends to answer ahead of a decisive Test against England at Twickenham this weekend.

New Zealand were beaten by a remarkable Welsh performance in the penultimate round of Nations Championship pool play that made more tackles than any team before them in Test history, but also came out of the gates firing on attack under the roof at Principality Stadium.

The All Blacks spent most of the final quarter of the Test pummeling the Welsh line, but were given no reward as Wales repelled their efforts and held them up any time they crossed the whitewash. The defensive display earned Ryan’s praise, but it was his side’s lack of energy that he kept coming back to in his immediate post-game reaction.

“It’s disappointing. It’s going to hurt for a while, that one,” Ryan told Jason Pine on Newstalk ZB shortly after the final whistle in Cardiff. “We just didn’t finish the opportunities we had, and they started the game with more intensity than us, and then started the second half with more intensity than us.

“And then, effectively, their defence, we just couldn’t break them down. Credit to them, and they deserve their win.”

Ryan said that after the slow start and Wales taking the lead, his players “went into their shells a little”, keeping Wales on top in the Test.

“We just didn’t come out of the blocks. We did the short kick-off and never regained that, and then they converted straight away and got momentum and bang. Teams score so fast now. But we were under pressure, and we couldn’t get ourselves out of it. And that’s probably the most disappointing thing.

“I’m just disappointed because we can’t hide from the fact that there are potentially parts in that game we’d have to question, mentally, if we were there. I think last week was a massive emotional week for us as a whole team and a whole group, and potentially we might have just been a little bit blasé of how we rolled up into Cardiff and got smacked for it.”

The team is still grieving the unexpected loss of their head of security, Logan Cadwallader, who had been with them for 10 years.

Ryan was adamant the All Blacks did not underestimate Wales’ quality, but admitted they did make life difficult for themselves with their selections. With an inaugural Nations Championship final now just two weeks away, the forwards coach was eager to rebound swiftly.

“Oh no, I don’t think it’s complacency. I just think they started and we just couldn’t pull them back, and that is what it is. We’ve got to move forward. We’ve got to move forward quickly.

“We also made a lot of changes; I think it was 10 that we made, and that’s cohesion. We gave a lot of fellas an opportunity, and there are some pretty good boys sitting in the stands, experience-wise, and potentially we lacked a bit of that at the end as well.

“I think we just have to have a look at it and just see where we were mentally; how we started the Test match.

“You’ve got to say that some of the defensive sets that Wales did were honestly quite unbelievable, and they were pretty spirited, and they hung in there and hung in there, and we just couldn’t break them down. So credit to them, they deserve that one.”

title: USA U20 star among four uncapped players in Australia’s Dubai Sevens squad
article_text:
USA Under-20s centre Dane Mitchell and former Moana Pasifika outside back Denzel Samoa are set to make their Australia Sevens debuts next week, with four uncapped players named to play at the HSBC SVNS Series season opener in Dubai.

Global Youth Sevens standout Bailey Roberts-Lintmeijer and ACT Brumbies prospect Chayse Geros have also been selected. Coach Liam Barry has otherwise gone with a fairly experienced group, which boasts a combined 235 SVNS events between them.

Mitchell made five appearances for the USA at the World Rugby Junior World Championship in Georgia, which included a few starts. But after returning to Australia, the university student got a chance to trial for the sevens side, which has opened the door to travelling the world.

Three-time Olympian Henry Hutchison is the most experienced member of the squad, having played at 68 tournaments, which Maurice Longbottom and James Turner bring more leadership to the national team.

Nathan Lawson is back with the sevens side after a stint in the NRL, having played a handful of matches for the St George Illawarra Dragons. Ben Dalton and Jayden Blake are others who have played in at least 10 events.

Australia will be without a few big-name players for the first stop of the season, with Henry Paterson still sidelined with a knee injury. Will Cartwright (knee) and Ben Dowling (foot) are also unavailable for selection.

“The squad has had a good few weeks in preparation and we are looking forward to our first tournament in Dubai,” Australia Men’s Sevens coach Liam Barry said.

“The 2026/2027 season has the added factor of Olympic qualification so we are well aware of the importance of getting off to a good start.”

Australia kick off their SVNS Series against the USA, South Africa and Argentina, If selected, Mitchell could potentially debut in the green and gold against the United States – who he was eligible for due to his mother.

The Aussies finished the 2025/26 SVNS Series strong with a drought-breaking title in Valladolid. SVNS Series action is stopping by the same destinations as last season, with Cape Town, Singapore, Perth, New York and Vancouver hosting regular season stops.

It’s a particularly important season with the top four teams securing automatic qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The World Championship heads to Hong Kong China, Valladolid and Bordeaux.

title: Wallaroos breakout star set for Australia Sevens debut in Dubai
article_text:
World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year nominee Amelia Whitaker will soon fly to Dubai as the only uncapped player in the Australia Women’s Sevens side, who are looking to win the HSBC SVNS Series event for the sixth time in seven years.

Whitaker was named the NSW Waratahs Player of the Year after a stellar Super Rugby Women’s campaign, and the winger was rewarded with higher Wallaroos honours. The 20-year-old rounded out a career-best 15s season with some stellar performances against Scotland.

Prolific Wallaroos try-scorers Desiree Miller and Maya Stewart were joined in the back three by Whitaker, who received Player of the Match honours after scoring two tries in a 56-12 win over Scotland at Sydney’s Accor Stadium.

The Wallaroos kicked off a historic quadruple header at Stadium Australia, with all four Teams in Gold taking the field. Australia faced arch-rivals the Black Ferns Sevens for the third time in less than 24 hours, while Whitaker celebrated with the Wallaroos.

Those SVNS Series players are now Whitaker’s teammates, with Isabella Nasser captaining a side that boasts World Championship-winning experience. Australia took out titles in Valladolid and Bordeaux earlier this year, as they pipped New Zealand in the race for the circuit’s top prize.

Maddison Levi is nearing the all-time try-scoring on the SVNS Series, with the recent Wallaroos debutant looking to chase down New Zealand’s Michalea Brake, who was named in the Black Ferns Sevens squad on Wednesday.

Tia Hinds, Heidi Dennis, Amahli Hala, Teagan Levi, Kaitlin Shave, Kahli Henwood, Bienne Terita, Ruby Nicholas, Kiiahla Duff and Alysia Lefau-Fakosilea have been named. MacKenzie Davis and Faith Nathan are unavailable due to injury.

“The team has had a strong preparation, with plenty of rugby played in different competitions and environments as well as two high-level tournaments together as a squad,” coach Reg Tayler said.

“We have benefited from these experiences and have been able to bring them back some learnings into our environment.

“We’ve got a good balance of youth and experience, and we’re heading to Dubai and Cape Town to set the standard.”

Australia started their SVNS Series matches against France, the USA and Spain in pool play. While New Zealand are the defending champions, the Aussies had won five straight titles at the event before that.

title: Springboks coach invites fans to watch party amid six-game ban
article_text:
Rassie Erasmus has issued an invite to Springboks fans to join a watch party he is hosting online for South Africa’s Nations Championship test against Ireland.

The coach is unable to attend the match due to a six-game ban he copped after a match-fixing rant following South Africa’s loss to France last week.

Under the rules of the ban, he will be unable to enter the stadium, communicate directly or indirectly with players or members of his staff during the match.

The ban will be in effect until a misconduct hearing is conducted per the request of South Africa Rugby. That will not happen before the Ireland game, though.

It is not the first time the outspoken coach has been hit with a ban for his explosive comments, but this time around he is taking a different approach to keep track of his team’s performance and also engage the fans.

The answer: a virtual watch party with the fans.

“Can sit and moan or make the best of it,” Erasmus wrote on X.

“I’ll be watching the match at the hotel, not keen to watch on my own. So let’s give it a go and hope I get the tech sorted – TV on, my laptop camera on and you’re welcome to join me.”

The website for the game-day watch along states the livestream is not an official Springbok or South Africa Rugby event.

Erasmus reiterated it is a “personal, not official” event on his social media pages, inviting fans over the age of 18 to join the stream.

The Springboks will face Ireland at 3.40am AEDT on Sunday, November 22.

title: Henry Pollock dropped as England team to face All Blacks is leaked
article_text:
Henry Pollock is set to drop to the bench as Steve Borthwick rings the changes for England’s blockbuster clash with the All Blacks on Saturday.

According to Telegraph Sport, Borthwick is expected to return to the bulk of the starting XV that defeated Australia 45-22 earlier this month.

Will Joseph is the notable exception, retaining his place on the wing following his sensational five-try performance against Japan.

The youngster replaces the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and is in line to win just his third England cap.

Fin Smith is expected to replace George Ford at fly-half, with Jack van Poortvliet making his sixth successive start at scrum-half.

Seb Atkinson and George Furbank have both recovered from injury and are tipped to return at inside centre and full-back respectively.

That means Max Ojomoh and Freddie Steward look set to miss out on starting spots despite impressing against Japan.

Borthwick is seemingly loading his bench with dynamite.

Pollock, Ellis Genge, Luke Cowan-Dickie, George Martin and Greg Fisilau are all expected to be named among the replacements, according to the Telegraph's team news.

Ollie Chessum returns at blindside flanker, with Ben Curry at openside and Ben Earl switching back to number eight.

Fin Baxter, Jamie George and Joe Heyes are expected to form the starting front row.

England will fancy their chances against an All Blacks side battling an injury crisis following their shock defeat to Wales.

Both teams will officially confirm their selections on Thursday.

Likely replacements: Luke Cowan-Dickie, Ellis Genge, George Martin, Henry Pollock and Greg Fisilau.

Asher Opoku-Fordjour and Will Stuart are competing for the replacement tighthead spot.

Think you could build a better XV than Borthwick? Take on our Ultimate Rugby Draft, select your dream team from current stars and legends, and see where you rank on our leaderboard.

title: England Grand Slam winner set for Ireland debut this weekend
article_text:
An England Grand Slam winner has been included in Ireland XV's squad for their clash with Fijian Latui this weekend.

Head coach Mark Sexton has named his side for Friday night's fixture in Cork, with a mixture of experienced internationals and emerging players set to feature.

The match, which forms part of a double-header at Virgin Media Park alongside Ireland U20s' meeting with Scotland U20s, offers players an opportunity to showcase their ability in an environment close to the senior international set-up.

One of the biggest names in the squad is former England international Kieran Brookes, who has been selected at tighthead prop.

The 36-year-old is in line to make his first appearance in an Ireland shirt in more than 15 years, having previously represented the country at U18, U19 and U20 level.

Brookes has made an impressive start since joining Munster this summer and qualifies for Ireland through his grandparents, who were born in Belfast and Dublin.

Born in England, Brookes began his professional career with Newcastle Falcons before joining Leicester Tigers in 2011.

He later returned to Newcastle before signing for Northampton Saints in 2015, where he became a regular starter.

A move to Wasps followed in 2018, before he headed to France to join Toulon in 2021. Three years later, he signed for Perpignan to continue his career in the Top 14.

However, his spell in France ended earlier than planned this summer after he agreed to terminate his contract a year early to join Munster.

The move to Limerick has now opened the door to a potential return to international rugby, this time with Ireland.

He also featured in the 2016 Six Nations, returning from injury to play a part in England's Grand Slam-winning campaign.

His final appearance for England came in 2016, meaning he has long since completed World Rugby's three-year stand-down period required to switch international allegiance.

However, until his move to Munster, Brookes had never played his club rugby in Ireland, meaning he did not meet the necessary eligibility requirements.

His arrival at Munster has changed that, giving the experienced prop a route back into international rugby.

At 36, he could provide valuable depth and leadership to Ireland's front row if he makes a successful return to the Test international stage.

There is also a familiar face in the Irish coaching set-up.

Current head coach Andy Farrell was part of Stuart Lancaster's England coaching team during Brookes' international career, meaning the pair have previously worked together at Test level.

Former England international Dan Kelly has been named on the bench, although he has featured for Ireland A in the past, starting against Spain and England A last season.

Ireland XV: 15 Todd Lawlor, 14 Finn Treacy, 13 James Hume, 12 Cathal Forde, 11 Daniel Ryan, 10 Joey Carbery, 9 Fintan Gunne, 1 Alex Usanov, 2 Gus McCarthy (c), 3 Kieran Brookes, 4 Fineen Wycherley, 5 Edwin Edogbo, 6 David McCann, 7 Will Connors, 8 Brian Gleeson.

Replacements: 16 Eoin de Buitléar, 17 Jeremy Loughman, 18 Jack Aungier, 19 Conor O’Tighearnaigh, 20 Paul Boyle, 21 Matthew Devine, 22 Jack Murphy, 23 Dan Kelly.

title: Tonight's rugby news as South African government steps in after World Rugby ban
article_text:
These are your headlines on the evening of Wednesday, November 18.

Rassie Erasmus has received the backing of the South African minister of sport, arts and culture following his six-match ban from World Rugby.

The Springboks head coach has been suspended by the game's governing body following inflammatory remarks he made in a press conference in Dublin on Monday.

His comments centred on the match officials following the defeat to France last week; Erasmus questioned the officiating during the game, suggesting there could have been manipulation of the match after claiming French players had committed 17 knee-drop tackles without intervention from the television match official. He even asked the question: "Is that not match-fixing?"

That led to World Rugby taking swift action and banning the double World Cup winner for the next six matches. He's now requested a full hearing.

Gayton McKenzie has now weighed in on the matter, saying Erasmus "foolishly" said what others were thinking and that he has his "full support".

“@RassieRugby foolishly and openly said what most of us have been saying amongst friends, he is passionate about the game, he has my full support,” McKenzie wrote on X.

“I know he feels that he let us down but maybe just maybe fairness shall return because of his outburst. We love you to the moon and back or should I say six matches and back.”

South Africa said in their request to World Rugby: “SA Rugby is requesting a full misconduct hearing for Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus following his sanctioning by an independent World Rugby panel for comments made in a press conference in Dublin on Monday.

“A SA Rugby spokesperson said that the organisation respected the process but had requested an opportunity for its coach to contextualize his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives.

“SA Rugby trusted that such a hearing could be expedited considering the seriousness of the charge, and will not make any further comment until the hearing could be completed.”

Gareth Thomas admits he has spent the days since Wales' stunning victory over New Zealand watching supporters' reactions on social media, saying the scenes across the country made him "feel like a fan".

The loosehead was at the heart of a remarkable defensive effort as Steve Tandy's side held out for a famous 35-28 victory over the All Blacks in Cardiff, resulting in one of the most remarkable upsets in Welsh rugby history.

When Peter Lakai crossed with 53 minutes on the clock at the Principality Stadium, there was a sense of inevitability about what would follow.

The All Blacks would come and do what they have done so many times in Cardiff and pull away to add another year onto the 73-year undefeated streak against Wales.

One man at the heart of a resilient Welsh defence that ensured no more points were scored was Thomas.

Thomas says "he feels like a fan" after watching Welsh public reaction to the famous win.

"It's a very special feeling. I was sat in bed last night, just watching the videos of reactions in pubs and places around Wales," he said. "I love it how it made everyone feel, what it meant to people.

"I had a message saying how special it made their 92-year-old friend and he's happy to go to the grave now after that. So special to make people feel like that.

"We can't stop watching the reactions because it makes you feel like a fan. I would love to have been a fan watching it, shows what it means to see ex-players with tears in their eyes."

With the Wallabies next up in Cardiff this weekend, Thomas says there is belief within the squad and that "eyes are on" their next opponents.

"There's a lot of belief in this group and we feel that's the sort of performance we can put in," he added. "To get that result will probably put a bit of expectation on us now, but we look forward to carrying that in terms of a performance that we want to live up to

"We are very aware of another big test on Saturday. Eyes are on Australia and we are going full steam into that. Mentally I've been impressed with how quickly we've moved on to this next job and we really want to back it up come Saturday."

Jamie Dobie is relishing the prospect of seeing fellow Glasgow back Josh McKay make his Scotland debut against Japan this weekend.

The New Zealand-born full-back, 29, becomes eligible this week to represent his adopted nation after fulfilling the five-year residency rule.

McKay, a key player for Glasgow since joining in November 2021, has been training with Gregor Townsend’s squad this month in preparation for potential involvement in Saturday’s Nations Championship clash at Murrayfield.

“I think he can add a lot,” said Dobie, who has been a team-mate of McKay’s throughout his time at Warriors. “Everybody’s seen what he’s been capable of in a Glasgow jersey over the last few seasons and since he’s been in Scotland.

“Even just having him around the group, he’s brought a real fresh energy and he’s such a good bloke to have in the squad. The guys at Glasgow have appreciated that for a good few years now.

“It’s great to see him in this environment and being able to add that and everybody knows the threat that he is on the pitch with ball in hand.

title: Newcastle expect big recruitment drive after England breakthrough
article_text:
Calum MacRae admits that Max Hicks’ Nations Championship call-up to the England squad will prove a useful selling point when it comes to selling a move to Newcastle Red Bulls to homegrown talent.

New Zealand-born Hicks, who qualifies to play for England through his Cornish mother, made his England A debut in the 59-24 home win over an Argentina XV in Bath a couple of weeks ago.

The Red Bulls summer signing from Perpignan, who was a second-half replacement in the West Country, was called up for training before last weekend’s win over Japan, and MacRae says it is useful to have examples of what can be achieved when speaking to players.

“It’s ultimately in these situations you need examples of it living and breathing, because it’s easy to say those things, but right from the get-go in the first block, we’ve got players who are in the conversation for international stuff, having just come in.

“So when you’re having those conversations in recruitment, it’s far easier to say what you’ve done rather than what you would like to do, and Max is a great example of that. There are a number of other guys in the conversation.

“Obviously, Ollie Leatherbarrow has been at the club for a period of time, but he has got an international cap with Scotland. Yes, it’s the other side of the border. But ultimately, it does show the quality of the programme that the club are putting together.

“It validates that if you come to Newcastle, not only can you perform and play well for the club, but that’s not a limiting factor if you’ve got aspirations to play international rugby,” said MacRae.

Red Bulls defence coach MacRae, who himself was a summer arrival in the North-East from Benetton, isn’t surprised that Hicks has hit the ground running and so quickly forced his way into Steve Borthwick’s thinking.

“As you’re coming to a new club, you do obviously do a bit of background, and everybody I touched base with spoke very, very highly about him and about his rugby ability.

“You can see he’s a real full-court player, both in attack and defence. He’s shown some brilliant work, ball in hand, soft skills on the offload, but also physically; he’s really shown in the last few weeks that he can impose himself physically. And also, he’s got an engine in some of the scramble efforts and some of the games where we’ve been put under pressure.

“He’s one of those guys that’s like a Duracell bunny that appears in situations where you need him when you’re put under pressure. So I think it’s fully deserved that he’s in the conversation for next-level honours.

“It has come quickly, but I think it’s merited because his performances suggest that he should be in those conversations. And it’s really positive from an England point of view that they’re prepared to actually pick players on form from the domestic competition,” he added.

title: Prem opens registration for expansion to 12 teams
article_text:
Prem Rugby has opened a registration process for teams to apply with the aim of expanding the league to 12 clubs for the 2029-30 season.

Plans to grow the league from the current 10 clubs were confirmed in February, with a request for information stage now open until 1 February 2027.

Clubs, investors and their authorised representatives have been invited to register their interest in joining the English top tier, although a statement said that no formal bid or commitment to invest is required to do so.

"As we celebrate our 30th season the Prem is in a strong position to grow as we look to write a new chapter with new clubs and new stories," said chief executive officer Simon Massie-Taylor.

"Expansion is a unique opportunity to welcome new audiences and clubs and we want to hear from anyone who shares our ambition to make the Gallagher Prem the best league in the world."

Massie-Taylor is currently in the United States along with Charlotte Samuelson, Prem chief operating officer, and representatives of investment group CVC, who own a minority stake in the league, meeting with global investors.

The Prem has consisted of 10 clubs since the 2022-23 season, when Wasps, Worcester and London Irish all folded within the space of a few months.

Promotion and relegation to and from the league was also scrapped as of this season, although no team had gone up or down since Saracens were relegated in 2020 for salary cap breaches and promoted back from the Championship the following season.

Previous conditions said teams would need to compete in the Champ for a season before being eligible to play in the Prem and that any bids would be assessed on a range of criteria including finances, investment potential, infrastructure and how their geographical base could help spread the Prem's appeal.

Earlier this month Rugby Football Union (RFU) chief executive Bill Sweeney confirmed that the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) had asked to join the Prem and form an Anglo-Welsh league.

Wales currently has four professional sides - Scarlets, Ospreys, Cardiff and Dragons - who play in the United Rugby Championship, although the WRU plans to cut one of the teams due to financial issues.

However, a statement from Prem Rugby and the RFU in October said that the focus was on expanding the league with English clubs.

"Resources are currently focused on supporting English clubs throughout the pyramid who aspire to join the league," they said.

Sweeney confirmed just over a week later that they had been approached by the WRU and that discussions would continue.

"We have been approached [by the WRU] and it is responsible for us to go back and ask more questions," he said.

title: Rassie Erasmus breaks silence after World Rugby ban
article_text:
Rassie Erasmus has broken his silence after being handed a six-match suspension by World Rugby.

The Springboks head coach was banned following comments he made about match officials in the aftermath of Friday’s defeat to France.

Erasmus questioned whether officials ignoring foul play could amount to manipulating international results, prompting World Rugby to investigate his remarks.

An independent disciplinary panel ruled that his comments suggested officials had either acted with bias or deliberately influenced the outcome of the match.

The panel deemed his remarks an unacceptable attack on the credibility and competence of match officials, triggering an automatic six-match suspension under World Rugby’s new Match Official Abuse Sanction Process.

The ban takes immediate effect. Erasmus is prohibited from coaching, communicating with players or management, entering match-day areas or carrying out media duties during international fixtures.

It is the third time he has been suspended for criticising officials, following previous bans in 2021 and 2022.

SA Rugby have confirmed they are requesting a full misconduct hearing.

The disciplinary problems continued for South Africa today, with Jasper Wiese also receiving a four-match ban.

The number eight initially received a yellow card against France, which was subsequently upgraded to a 20-minute red card for making contact with an opponent above the line of the shoulders in a ruck.

With South Africa set to face Ireland at the Aviva Stadium this weekend, the latest setbacks leave them with a major challenge.

The Springboks are targeting top spot in the southern hemisphere table ahead of next weekend’s Nations Championship finals weekend, but will now have to do so without two key figures.

Erasmus has now taken to X to address the suspension for the first time, posting a rather unusual message to his followers.

"Can sit and moan or make the best of it. I’ll be watching the match at the hotel. Not keen to watch in on my own. So lets give it a go and hope I get the “tech” sorted = TV on, My Laptop camera on, and you’re welcome to join me. Sign up here (adults 18+): http://watchwithrassie.com. This is personal, not official."

The exact meaning behind the post remains unclear, but it appears to be Erasmus' response to his suspension, with the Springboks boss seemingly inviting supporters to join him virtually while he watches the Ireland match.

On the website linked, it says, "I'll be watching Saturday's game, and I'd rather not do it alone. If you'd like to watch with me, sign up below.

"We each watch on our own TV, and I'll be on camera so you can see me watch it too. Send me a message and I'll read some out."

There is also a song title, "Badge of Hard Yard."

title: Two ex-England internationals in Ireland XV team, one set for debut
article_text:
Former England international Kieran Brookes is set to make his Ireland XV debut after being named to start against Fijian Latui in Cork on Friday.

The Munster prop has been selected at tighthead by head coach Mark Sexton for the clash at Virgin Media Park, forming a front-row alongside Leinster pair Alex Usanov and captain Gus McCarthy.

Brookes, who represented England 16 times over a decade ago, is one of several experienced names included in the side, with the 37-cap Joey Carbery starting at fly-half and linking up with Leinster scrum-half Fintan Gunne.

James Hume and Cathal Forde have been paired in the centres, while Todd Lawlor, Finn Treacy and Daniel Ryan form the back three.

There is also significant Test experience throughout the squad, with McCarthy one of eight members of the matchday 23 who have previously played international rugby for Ireland.

Fineen Wycherley and Edwin Edogbo form an all-Munster second row, while David McCann starts at blindside flanker, Will Connors at openside and Brian Gleeson at No.8.

The fixture has been positioned as an opportunity for players of national interest to experience the standards and environment of the senior Ireland set-up, while also giving a number of emerging prospects an opportunity to push their case.

Another former England international, Dan Kelly, is among the replacements alongside Jack Murphy and Matthew Devine, with Eoin de Buitléar, Jeremy Loughman, Jack Aungier, Conor O’Tighearnaigh and Paul Boyle providing the forward cover.

The match forms part of a double-header at Virgin Media Park, with Ireland U20 facing Scotland U20 earlier in the day.

Ireland XV: 15 Todd Lawlor, 14 Finn Treacy, 13 James Hume, 12 Cathal Forde, 11 Daniel Ryan, 10 Joey Carbery, 9 Fintan Gunne, 1 Alex Usanov, 2 Gus McCarthy (c), 3 Kieran Brookes, 4 Fineen Wycherley, 5 Edwin Edogbo, 6 David McCann, 7 Will Connors, 8 Brian Gleeson.

Replacements: 16 Eoin de Buitléar, 17 Jeremy Loughman, 18 Jack Aungier, 19 Conor O’Tighearnaigh, 20 Paul Boyle, 21 Matthew Devine, 22 Jack Murphy, 23 Dan Kelly.

title: PREM Rugby expansion plans take next step with bidding announcement
article_text:
The race to join an expanded PREM Rugby heated up on Wednesday after the league opened its doors to expressions of interest.

England's top flight rugby union league is looking to expand by two, from 10 to 12, for the start of the 2029-30 season and this week invited ambitious parties to declare their interest.

Several clubs from outside Prem Rugby have told City AM they are exploring expressions of interest.

It comes as the league's chief Simon Massie-Taylor woos potential investors in the United States, as revealed by City AM last month.

"As we celebrate our 30th season the Prem is in a strong position to grow as we look to write a new chapter with new clubs and new stories," he said in New York.

"Expansion is a unique opportunity to welcome new audiences and clubs and we want to hear from anyone who shares our ambition to make the Gallagher Prem the best league in the world."

The window is open until the beginning of February ahead of a full tender process, while those expressing interest between now and next spring will not need to make a formal bid of investment.

There had been interest in joining Prem Rugby from teams in Wales, but figures within the English game have said they will prioritise teams in the RFU pyramid, as well as bids from the likes of former stalwarts London Irish and Wasps.

Irish, who were last month acquired by rugby-loving Essex energy entrepreneur Steve Daniels, are set to lodge their interest in joining an expanded Prem Rugby, while similar interest is expected to be shown by Christopher Holland – the owner of both Champ Rugby team Worcester Warriors and the intellectual property of Wasps.

There is an expectation that Ealing Trailfinders, Cornish Pirates and other mainstays of the second tier will show interest to stay in the mix for promotion and fend off phoenix clubs looking to come back into the pyramid at the highest level.

The expansion plans come amid a flurry of investment into Prem Rugby from the likes of Red Bull, Sir James Dyson and Bill Foley's Black Knight. Gloucester Rugby, Northampton Saints and Leicester Tigers are among the clubs currently said to be in active investment talks.

title: Springboks rocked by new ban 24 hours after World Rugby suspend Rassie Erasmus
article_text:
South Africa forward Jasper Wiese has been handed a four-week suspension following his 20-minute red card against France, with the punishment coming amid fresh disciplinary controversy surrounding the Springboks.

Wiese was sent off during South Africa's 21-19 defeat at the Stade de France on Friday, November 13, after initially receiving a yellow card for a dangerous clear-out in a ruck.

The sanction was subsequently upgraded to a 20-minute red card for making contact with an opponent's head.

A World Rugby Foul Play Review Committee, chaired by Scotland's Roddy MacLeod, considered the incident and imposed a four-week suspension, having determined that it warranted a mid-range entry point sanction.

The committee took into account Wiese's previous disciplinary record, including earlier instances of similar offences, although it also noted that the forward had demonstrated remorse and admitted his guilt.

Wiese has accepted the punishment, which will see him miss South Africa's Nations Championship clash with Ireland on November 21 and the competition's finals weekend on November 28 or 29.

He will also miss two Japanese club fixtures for Urayasu D-Rocks against Canon Eagles on December 4 and Panasonic Wild Knights on December 12.

The 30-year-old does have the option of undertaking World Rugby's Coaching Intervention Programme, with successful completion reducing his suspension from four weeks to three.

The disciplinary decision comes just a day after Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus was handed a six-match suspension by World Rugby over comments he made about match officials following the defeat to France.

Erasmus questioned the officiating during the game, suggesting there could have been manipulation of the match after claiming French players had committed 17 knee-drop tackles without intervention from the television match official. He even asked the question: "Is that not match-fixing?"

World Rugby ruled that his comments crossed the threshold for serious misconduct, determining that they questioned the integrity of match officials.

South African Rugby has since confirmed it will request a full misconduct hearing to allow Erasmus to explain his remarks.

title: Nations Championship over for Bok Jasper Wiese after ban
article_text:
South Africa No.8 Jasper Wiese will miss the remainder of the Nations Championship after receiving a four-week suspension following his 20-minute red card against France.

The Springbok was initially shown a yellow card early in the second half of South Africa’s defeat to Les Bleus at the Stade de France on Friday for making direct contact to the head of French centre Kalvin Gourgues at a ruck. The decision was then upgraded to a 20-minute red card for a breach of Law 9.20b, relating to dangerous play in a ruck or maul.

A Foul Play Review Committee, chaired by Scotland’s Roddy MacLeod alongside Aggrey Chabeda of Kenya and New Zealand’s Ofisa Tonu, determined that the offence warranted the mid-range entry point of four weeks.

The panel considered TMO footage, match official reports and player statements in reaching its decision, while Wiese’s previous disciplinary record, including similar offences, was also taken into account. His admission of guilt and demonstration of remorse were considered as mitigating factors.

Wiese has accepted the sanction and will consequently miss Saturday’s Nations Championship meeting with Ireland as well as South Africa’s match at the Nations Championship Finals on the last weekend of November.

The 31-year-old will also be unavailable for Urayasu D-Rocks’ opening two fixtures of the Japan Rugby League One season against Canon Eagles on December 4 and Panasonic Wild Knights on December 12.

However, Wiese has the option of undertaking World Rugby’s Coaching Intervention Programme, which would reduce his suspension from four weeks to three if completed successfully.

That would remove the Panasonic Wild Knights fixture from his suspension, although it would not alter his availability for the Springboks, bringing his Nations Championship campaign to an end regardless.

Wiese has become a key figure in South Africa’s pack, but Rassie Erasmus will now have to look elsewhere at No.8 for the remainder of the competition as the Springboks prepare to face Ireland before heading into the Nations Championship Finals.

title: PREM Rugby in talks with potential USA investors as expansion plans laid out
article_text:
PREM Rugby CEO Simon Massie-Taylor and Chief Operating Officer Charlotte Samuelson are both in New York this week speaking to investors who have shown an interest in English club rugby’s premier competition.

American billionaire Bill Foley bought out Exeter Chiefs through his firm Black Knight Rugby in June 2026, and it is hoped that others will follow suit following the league’s shift to a franchise-based system protected against relegation.

Red Bull are into their second season as owners of Newcastle, Sir James Dyson now co-owns Bath with fellow multi-millionaire Bruce Craig and Northampton and Gloucester have both benefitted from a fresh injection of funds now that there is more security.

Currently a 10-team league, the plan is to add two more teams to the PREM in time for the start of the 2029/30 season, and the process for doing that is now underway.

Ambitious clubs, investors and their authorised representatives are being invited to register their interest in joining the Gallagher PREM.

The Request for Information (RFI) stage is an opportunity for investors to sell their vision to the league, outlining what value they’d add to the league, and it is open until 1 February 2027 with a tender process to follow later that year.

PREM CEO Simon Massie-Taylor said: “As we celebrate our 30th season the PREM is in a strong position to grow as we look to write a new chapter with new clubs and new stories.

“Expansion is a unique opportunity to welcome new audiences and clubs and we want to hear from anyone who shares our ambition to make the Gallagher PREM the best league in the world.”

One-time PREM finalists London Irish would appear to be likely candidates following a recent change of ownership.

A month ago, Gamechanger Investments Limited completed the acquisition of the club’s name, brand and associated intellectual property and look deadset on restoring the club’s fortunes.

Worcester, who won the Champ in their first season back from oblivion, are also likely to be seriously considering applying for a place in an expanded 12-team league.

title: Every nation banned from the Rugby World Cup – including the Springboks
article_text:
With tensions between the Springboks and World Rugby reaching boiling point following Rassie Erasmus' six-match ban, we look back at the nations previously shut out of rugby's biggest tournament.

Erasmus was handed an immediate suspension by World Rugby following his controversial comments about match officials.

SA Rugby has since requested a full misconduct hearing.

However, the Springboks themselves have previously been excluded from rugby's biggest competition, missing the first two editions of the Rugby World Cup.

From passport scandals to political boycotts, several other nations have also seen their World Cup dreams disappear.

RUCK looks back at the countries banned, excluded or kicked out of World Cup contention.

Paraguay were within touching distance of a historic first World Cup appearance when disaster struck.

Having beaten Brazil in a two-legged play-off, they discovered they had fielded an ineligible player.

Paraguay voluntarily withdrew from the final qualification tournament, with World Rugby confirming Brazil as their replacement.

Belarus were suspended from international rugby in February 2022 following the country's support for Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

Although they have never appeared at a Rugby World Cup, the suspension prevented them from entering qualification for Australia 2027.

Nigeria's World Cup ambitions were ended by a dispute away from the pitch.

Rugby Africa suspended the country's union following government interference in its administration.

As a result, Nigeria missed out on the African pre-qualification process for the 2023 tournament.

Tahiti celebrated a famous 13-9 victory over the Cook Islands during qualification for the 2019 World Cup.

They had fielded two ineligible players.

The result was overturned, with the Cook Islands advancing instead.

Belgium were caught up in one of the biggest eligibility scandals in rugby history.

They were docked 30 qualification points for fielding ineligible players across six matches.

However, unlike Romania and Spain, Belgium had not secured a World Cup or play-off spot before the punishment.

Romania thought they had secured their ticket to Japan before an eligibility scandal turned their world upside down.

A 30-point deduction cost them their automatic qualification place, with Russia taking their spot.

Once is unfortunate. Twice is a nightmare.

Spain received a 40-point deduction during qualification for the 2019 tournament before suffering another eligibility setback four years later.

South African-born prop Gavin van den Berg was deemed ineligible, with Spain losing their place at the 2023 World Cup.

An investigation also uncovered alterations to stamps in the player's passport.

Spain's appeal failed, with Romania taking their place.

Russia were thrown out of qualification for the 2003 World Cup after fielding three ineligible South African-born players.

They were also hit with a hefty £75,000 fine.

Almost two decades later, Russia were suspended from international rugby following the invasion of Ukraine.

Their hopes of qualifying for the 2023 and 2027 tournaments were subsequently ended.

It is almost impossible to imagine a Rugby World Cup without the Springboks.

However, South Africa were excluded from the first two editions due to the international sporting boycott against apartheid.

They finally made their debut in 1995, hosting the tournament and famously defeating the All Blacks in the final.

The Springboks have since lifted the Webb Ellis Cup four times, making them the most successful nation in the competition's history.

They have already qualified for the 2027 tournament, with Erasmus' latest suspension applying to the coach rather than the national team.

title: Rob Baxter provides fresh update on Immanuel Feyi-Waboso
article_text:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter has revealed that star winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso is undergoing regular assessments for the ankle injury he picked up playing for England, but says it is too early to say when he will be back on the pitch.

Baxter confirmed that Feyi-Waboso didn’t need an operation after being injured in the first half of England’s 45-22 Nations Championship win over Australia at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium two weeks ago.

He says it is too early to determine when Feyi-Waboso will play again, but hopes it will be during the next block of fixtures, which starts with a trip to Sale Sharks on December 6.

“There is not an operation at this stage. Now it’s kind of coming down to that week by week, see where he goes as he strengthens. There’ll be like regular catch-ups with England and assessments as to where he goes and how he moves onto the next step.

“I think it’s a little bit probably like his hamstring with Manny. You don’t really know till you get a couple of weeks in, and then when you get a couple of weeks in, you start to know what the timescales are.”

Another Chiefs international who has been on the treatment table since the summer is Italian lineout specialist Andrea Zambonin, who is in the running to play against Gloucester in the PREM Rugby Cup on Saturday afternoon following a shoulder operation.

“He’s pretty close now. Zambo is in full training. Whether he’ll get any game this week or not, we’re still kind of just finalising things, but he’s very close now, which is good news,” added Baxter.

Baxter could also plunge former All Black Dallas McLeod into action for the first time when the Cherry and Whites visit Sandy Park, having given him a break following his exploits for Canterbury in the NPC and the Crusaders in Super Rugby.

“Dallas is looking very good. He has trained very well. We knew he’s a quality player and he’s trained like that. He’s now had that break from playing and obviously got himself up and running with how we want to play and what we want to do.

“I would now deem him fully available and ready to play with us as well,” said Baxter, who will name his team for the West Country derby on Friday lunchtime.

title: South Africa condemn online abuse of World Rugby officials following Rassie Erasmus ban
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

South Africa Rugby has condemned online abuse of World Rugby officials following the decision to hand Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus a six-match ban for questioning whether officiating during his side’s defeat by France amounted to match-fixing.

An independent panel imposed the punishment after reviewing comments made by Erasmus at a media conference on Monday ahead of the Nations Championship match against Ireland at the Aviva Stadium.

SA Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing for the 54-year-old, who will not be able to have any matchday involvement in international fixtures during the suspension.

Following a social media backlash against the global governing body, SA Rugby has called for calm to allow the proper processes to run their course.

“SA Rugby is aware of the extensive public commentary, analysis and debate surrounding recent matters involving Springbok head coach Rassie Erasmus and World Rugby,” a statement from the organisation read.

“We are mindful that a significant volume of commentary, opinion and AI-generated content is currently circulating in the public domain, much of which does not necessarily reflect the facts, context or processes involved.

“What is deeply concerning, however, is the reaction of some individuals on social media and other platforms, particularly reports of threats and abusive conduct directed at World Rugby officials and administrators.

“SA Rugby unequivocally condemns any form of intimidation, threats or personal attacks. Such behaviour has no place in rugby and is entirely contrary to the values upon which our game is founded.

“Rugby has long been recognised as a sport built on respect, discipline, integrity and sportsmanship. These values extend beyond the field of play and apply equally to players, coaches, match officials, administrators and supporters. While robust debate and differing opinions are part of sport, they must always be expressed respectfully and responsibly.

“SA Rugby also wishes to assure all stakeholders that rugby possesses the necessary expertise, experience and governance structures to deal with matters of this nature appropriately.

“Any issues that arise will be addressed through the established rugby processes and by the individuals entrusted with these responsibilities, ensuring that due process s followed and that the best interests of the game remain paramount.

“We remain committed to protecting the integrity of rugby, upholding its values and ensuring that all participants in the game are treated with dignity and respect.”

title: Nadine Roos leads injury returnees as Springboks target SVNS 2 success
article_text:
Springbok Women’s Sevens head coach Cecil Afrika has received a major boost ahead of the HSBC SVNS 2 campaign, with star playmaker Nadine Roos returning from injury.

Roos, named SA Rugby Women’s Player of the Year in 2025 after helping the Springbok Women reach their first-ever Women’s Rugby World Cup quarter-final, missed the majority of 2026 after suffering an injury in SVNS 2 action in March as the side placed third in Montevideo.

As a result, Roos missed HSBC SVNS World Championship events in Hong Kong, Valladolid and Bordeaux as the Springbok Women’s Sevens failed to get a top-eight finish and a HSBC SVNS Series spot.

“That was my first very serious injury, but I made peace with the injury early on,” Roos said.

“I realised that it would take a certain amount of time and managing the recovery was key. Returning to the field with the sevens squad – where my career started – was also a full circle moment for me.”

Roos is not the only returnee to the training pitch. Rights Mkhari, Liske Lategan, Leigh Fortuin, Shannon-Lee Windvogel and Kemisetso Baloyi have all made returns from long-term injury.

The group will now be available for the new SVNS 2 campaign, which starts in Nairobi this January. The group will then play events in Montevideo and São Paulo, with a top four finish securing a spot at World Championship events.

This year, a top eight finish after three World Championship legs can qualify teams for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

Minjon Ras, team doctor, said: “As a medical and rehabilitation team, we’re privileged to work with players who push boundaries and do everything they can to get back to the game they love ahead of schedule.

“Sometimes we have to rein in that eagerness, and sometimes they surprise us. What I admire most is how they trust the rehab process and respect the timeframes we set for them.”

title: Springboks hit out at 'threats and abusive conduct' in fresh public statement
article_text:
The South African Rugby Union has condemned a disturbing campaign of intimidation, threats and personal attacks directed at World Rugby officials and administrators by some of the country's own supporters.

Erasmus has been suspended for six matches by World Rugby following his comments in a press conference in Dublin on Monday where he questioned officiating and disciplinary decisions around the world champion's defeat to France last week, posing whether referees are "match-fixing".

An independent panel reviewed his comments and banned him for six games with immediate effect. He has now asked for a full misconduct hearing.

In the extraordinary press conference in the Irish capital, Erasmus claimed officials had missed 17 knee-drop tackles on his players against the French, suggested acts of foul play are not being picked up in what he called a "manipulation of the game", before adding that he felt referees were showing more leniency to sides from the northern hemisphere.

Following his ban high-ranking members of World Rugby have been the subject of intense criticism on social media.

"We are mindful that a significant volume of commentary, opinion and AI-generated content is currently circulating in the public domain, much of which does not necessarily reflect the facts, context or processes involved," read the statement.

"SA Rugby unequivocally condemns any form of intimidation, threats, or personal attacks. Such behaviour has no place in rugby and is entirely contrary to the values upon which our game is founded.

"Rugby has long been recognised as a sport built on respect, discipline, integrity, and sportsmanship. These values extend beyond the field of play and apply equally to players, coaches, match officials, administrators, and supporters.

"While robust debate and differing opinions are part of sport, they must always be expressed respectfully and responsibly.

"SA Rugby also wishes to assure all stakeholders that rugby possesses the necessary expertise, experience, and governance structures to deal with matters of this nature appropriately.

"Any issues that arise will be addressed through the established rugby processes and by the individuals entrusted with these responsibilities, ensuring that due process is followed and that the best interests of the game remain paramount.

"We remain committed to protecting the integrity of rugby, upholding its values, and ensuring that all participants in the game are treated with dignity and respect."

This is not the first time the double Rugby World Cup-winning coach has been in hot water with World Rugby.

During the 2021 British & Irish Lions tour of South Africa he was banned from all rugby activities for two months after releasing an hour-long video critiquing the referee's performance in the first Test.

title: Andy Farrell responds to controversial Springboks decision
article_text:
Ireland head coach Andy Farrell previously questioned a refereeing decision involving Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu when the two sides last faced each other.

There is already plenty of tension ahead of this weekend's Nations Championship showdown, with Springboks boss Rassie Erasmus set to serve a six-match ban following his criticism of match officials after their defeat to France.

Erasmus questioned whether officials overlooking foul play could amount to manipulating international results after South Africa's loss on Friday.

It is not the first time the Springboks coach has faced disciplinary action for his comments about referees, having also been suspended in 2021 and 2022.

World Rugby handed down the latest punishment after reviewing a series of remarks made by Erasmus during a media conference earlier this week, in which he questioned the standard of officiating.

With both sides fighting to finish top of their respective hemispheres, there is plenty riding on Saturday's encounter.

Their long-standing rivalry only adds to the occasion, with a hostile atmosphere expected at the Aviva Stadium.

However, their previous meeting in Dublin last year also left plenty of talking points.

South Africa claimed a 24-13 victory, but one incident involving fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu sparked considerable debate.

The South African escaped a yellow card after making a no-arms tackle on Ireland winger Tommy O'Brien, with contact made to the head.

Referee Matthew Carley decided against reaching for his cards, a decision that was questioned after the match.

Farrell was subsequently asked whether comments from the South African coaching staff, who had previously suggested their team were being unfairly treated by World Rugby, had influenced the officials.

"Well, we brought it up with the referees before the game and they said that would never be a factor, obviously, because this is a separate game.

Twelve months on, the controversy has taken another turn.

This time, it is South African supporters questioning the treatment their side received during Friday's defeat to France.

Many have also voiced their frustration at the six-match suspension handed to Erasmus, adding another layer of tension ahead of this weekend's clash with Ireland.

title: Rassie ban: SA Rugby condemns ‘threats and abusive conduct' directed at World Rugby officials
article_text:
SA Rugby has issued a statement condemning personal attacks on World Rugby officials in the wake of Rassie Erasmus’ six-match suspension.

The Springboks boss was banned by the game’s governing body following his remarks in a press conference criticising the refereeing performance in South Africa’s defeat to France, stating that 16/17 knee-drop tackles went unpunished.

He also said that Maxime Lucu’s sin-binning period was not a full 10-minute sanction. Erasmus highlighted a perceived unfairness in the way disciplinary hearings are conducted, pointing to the disparity in Jan-Hendrik Wessels and Tadhg Furlong’s sanctions over alleged groping, predicting that Sam Prendergast would be free to face South Africa this weekend, a prediction that has proven to be correct.

However, the remark that resulted in his ban was when Erasmus questioned whether the lack of punishment for the knee-drop tackles constituted match-fixing.

Unsurprisingly, the news of his suspension has not gone down well on social media, and SA Rugby has issued a statement addressing the backlash.

“SA Rugby is aware of the extensive public commentary, analysis and debate surrounding recent matters involving Springbok Head Coach Rassie Erasmus and World Rugby,” a statement read.

“We are mindful that a significant volume of commentary, opinion and AI-generated content is currently circulating in the public domain, much of which does not necessarily reflect the facts, context or processes involved.

“What is deeply concerning, however, is the reaction of some individuals on social media and other platforms, particularly reports of threats and abusive conduct directed at World Rugby officials and administrators.

“SA Rugby unequivocally condemns any form of intimidation, threats, or personal attacks. Such behaviour has no place in rugby and is entirely contrary to the values upon which our game is founded.

“Rugby has long been recognised as a sport built on respect, discipline, integrity, and sportsmanship. These values extend beyond the field of play and apply equally to players, coaches, match officials, administrators, and supporters. While robust debate and differing opinions are part of sport, they must always be expressed respectfully and responsibly.”

It concluded: “SA Rugby also wishes to assure all stakeholders that rugby possesses the necessary expertise, experience, and governance structures to deal with matters of this nature appropriately. Any issues that arise will be addressed through the established rugby processes and by the individuals entrusted with these responsibilities, ensuring that due process is followed and that the best interests of the game remain paramount.

“We remain committed to protecting the integrity of rugby, upholding its values, and ensuring that all participants in the game are treated with dignity and respect.”

This is the second statement that SA Rugby have issued following Erasmus’ suspension, after it confirmed that they have requested a full disciplinary process, as it will provide an opportunity for the head coach to ‘contextualize his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives’.

World Rugby has not yet confirmed when the process will commence, with Erasmus likely to be absent from the matchday proceedings on Saturday when South Africa face Ireland in Dublin on Saturday.

title: Ireland fly-half Prendergast cleared to face South Africa
article_text:
Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast has been cleared to play in Saturday's Nations Championship match against South Africa after a panel ruled his hip-drop tackle against Fiji was not worthy of a red card.

The 23-year-old was not punished on the pitch after he wrapped his body around the back of Fiji flanker Peceli Yato's legs in a first-half tackle.

Hip-drop tackles, when a tackling player drops their hips and bodyweight on to the ball-carrier's legs, were outlawed by World Rugby before November's internationals.

A citing commissioner, who reviews match action and recommends retrospective punishment if they believe any incident merits a red card, highlighted Prendergast's tackle.

But Ireland successfully argued that the incident did not meet the threshold for a red card, clearing their first-choice fly-half for the weekend's meeting.

Prendergast's case was under scrutiny after South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus predicted he would escape punishment on a "technicality".

"We are in the northern hemisphere. I think there is going to be a technicality and he is going to play," said Erasmus on Monday, adding that he thought Prendergast's tackle was "terrible".

In the same Dublin media conference, Erasmus claimed France had got away with 17 hip-drops or knee-drops (where a player tackles an opponent while having a knee on the floor) in the Springboks' 21-19 loss in Paris last Friday.

Erasmus targeted the television match official Matteo Liperini for criticism.

"I'm saying if he didn't see it, it must be a technology problem. If he saw it and decided not to act on it, is that not match-fixing?" Erasmus added.

Erasmus was banned for six Tests for his comments, with World Rugby saying his words constituted "an unacceptable attack on the credibility and competence of the match officials".

TMOs have been guided to only interrupt matches in cases of clear and obvious foul play as part of protocols agreed with head coaches, including Erasmus.

Erasmus' long list of grievances also includes Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong avoiding punishment for an alleged groin grab. South Africa front row Jan-Hendrik Wessels was handed a nine-match ban for a similar offence last year.

The 54-year-old has a history of criticising officials in public, having been banned for leaking an hour-long video pulling apart referee Nic Berry's performance in his team's first-Test defeat by the British and Irish Lions in 2021.

The following year, following a defeat by France, he posted a string of videos on social media questioning Wayne Barnes' decisions.

Both Berry and Barnes have spoken about the abuse they have received in the aftermath of Erasmus' criticisms.
