“To do whatever it takes to be in a good shape, to feel physically ready for a battle tomorrow.

“It’s gonna be a really important half a day that I have ahead of me with my team, with my physio, with the doctor.

“We will see, but I think I’m doing great things. I just felt great on court today, I tried not to move that much. I tried to be aggressive to dominate the match as much as I can, and I think I could do it.

“So, I’m just really happy that I’m getting more confident, the way that I’m hitting the ball, the way that I’m seeing what’s going on in the match. And after that, trying to find solutions.

“So, let’s see what’s going to happen tomorrow, but I’m really happy and proud about the level that I’m playing today, and the way that I’m feeling.”

Alcaraz will play world No 4 Ben Shelton in the semi-finals in Turin on Saturday.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion is on a 12-match winning streak, having secured titles at the Paris Masters and the Vienna Open at his previous two events.

The 23-year-old is vying for his first ATP Finals title.

title: Carlos Alcaraz injury update: Spaniard cancels ATP Finals warmup before Flavio Cobolli match
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz’s fitness at the 2026 ATP Finals continues to be a cause for concern after the Spaniard’s decision before his final round robin match.

World No 3 Alcaraz sustained a left hamstring injury during his 6-2, 6-4 victory over Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday afternoon in Turin.

Early in the second set of the match, Alcaraz took a medical timeout and had his left thigh area strapped.

In his post-match press conference, Alcaraz confirmed he had felt a “little problem” in his hamstring.

“Well, I feel it a little bit. I’m not gonna lie,” said the 23-year-old.

“But unfortunately I was, you know, I was playing great, and suddenly, I felt a little problem of my hamstring.”

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Alcaraz added: “Right now, I’m just feeling okay. We will see with my team, with my physio, but I think the rest of the day and tomorrow is really going to be important days ahead of me.”

The seven-time Grand Slam champion cancelled his practice session on Thursday and underwent an MRI scan on his hamstring at the Institute of Sports Medicine in Turin.

Following the scan, it was reported that Alcaraz would continue his ATP Finals campaign.

Alcaraz has already qualified for the semi-finals as the winner of the Ivan Lendl Group.

Prior to his victory over Medvedev, Alcaraz dismantled Frances Tiafoe 6-2, 6-2 in his opening match on Monday.

The reigning Australian Open champion will face Flavio Cobolli in his final round robin match on Friday afternoon.

It emerged on Friday morning that Alcaraz had cancelled his pre-match warmup, which had been scheduled for 10:45pm on Centre Court at the Inalpi Arena.

Alcaraz will instead have a short warmup around an hour before his match with Cobolli begins at 2pm local time.

The former world No 1, who is making his fourth appearance at the ATP Finals, is aiming to win his maiden title at the prestigious indoor event.

He was a runner-up at the 2025 edition of the ATP Finals, when he lost to his rival Jannik Sinner.

title: Arthur Fils & Rafael Jodar’s ATP Finals ranking points & prize money after round robin exits
article_text:
Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar have both been eliminated from the 2026 ATP Finals, but how many ranking points and how much prize money did they earn?

Jodar had to beat Ben Shelton on Thursday to keep his hopes of progressing to the semi-finals alive, but his 7-6(8), 7-5 defeat to the American meant he finished bottom of the John McEnroe Group.

The Spanish star’s loss to Shelton saw him finish with a 0-3 record after he was beaten by Alexander Zverev and Arthur Fils in his first two matches.

After Shelton’s victory over Jodar, Fils required a straight-set win over Zverev in the final match in the John McEnroe Group on Thursday evening to qualify for the last four.

However, Fils was eliminated as he suffered a 6-4, 7-6(4) defeat to the world No 1.

The Frenchman lost to Shelton in his opening match before defeating Jodar in his second.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Both Jodar and Fils were making their debuts at the ATP Finals.

Zverev won the John McEnroe Group with a 3-0 record, while Shelton finished in second place after winning two of his three matches.

Fils collected 200 ATP ranking points for his round robin win against Jodar. He has overtaken Flavio Cobolli to climb to a projected new career-high position of world No 6 in the ATP Live Rankings.

Jodar, meanwhile, did not add to his points tally after losing all three of his matches in Turin. He remains 10th in the rankings.

Both Fils and Jodar earned a participation fee of $338,000 for playing all of their round robin matches.

Fils earned an additional $405,000 for his victory.

title: Disappointing early exit for top seed Julien Carraggi
article_text:
It was a disappointing start to the Scottish Open for Belgium's Julien Carraggi, who entered this week's International Challenge tournament as the top seed but suffered a first-round defeat.

The charismatic Belgian was hoping for a strong run in Scotland, but his campaign came to an early end against South Korea's Hyeon Woo Cho, ranked world number 117.

Cho secured the victory in straight games, winning 21-13, 24-22, despite a much closer battle in the second game.

The result brings Carraggi's Scottish Open campaign to an end after just one match, while Cho continues his impressive form on the European circuit.

The Korean arrived in Scotland following an impressive performance at last week's Irish Open, where he reached the men's singles final.

There, he was defeated by Denmark's Victor Kaufmann, who claimed the title.

The Scottish Open continues throughout the weekend, with plenty of exciting matches and players to watch.

Among the home favourites are Scotland's Christopher Grimley/Matthew Grimley in the men's doubles, Julie MacPherson/Ciara Torrance in the women's doubles and Alexander Dunn/Julie MacPherson in the mixed doubles, all hoping to deliver strong performances in front of the home crowd.

Several other big European names are also competing in Scotland, including Denmark's Jesper Toft/Amalie Cecilie Kudsk in the mixed doubles, France's Julien Maio/William Villeger in the men's doubles, Finland's Joakim Oldorff and Germany's Yvonne Li in singles.

With these players and many more still in contention, there is plenty of badminton to look forward to as the tournament progresses.

Follow all the action live and for free on badmintoneurope.tv, where every match from the tournament is available to watch.

title: Patrick Reed is back on the PGA Tour. This time he's not fighting demons
article_text:
On your list of prominent, major-winning American PGA Tour golfers thinking about going LIV, Patrick Reed had to be about dead last, right alongside Tiger Woods. Right? We’re talking about Captain America, with his drumstick forearms and swaggery, toes-out walk. Yes, ole Pat Reed. He’s only 36, but he married young, had kids young and has always seemed mature beyond his years, except when he hasn’t.

Reed, born in Texas in 1990, was raised on TW (Tiger Woods), George W. (Bush) — and red meat. The main course at the Masters dinner Reed hosted in 2019 was prime bone-in cowboy rib eye, if that means anything to you. He has been known to fly freshly cut steaks into remote tournament sites. For years, he wore black-and-red on tourney Sundays, à la Tiger.

In his 20s, as a card-carrying Tour player, you’d see P. Reed parading through your better American country-club clubhouses in custom-made cowboy boots. He secured his Tour playing privileges by getting through six Monday qualifiers (unheard of) in a four-month period in 2012, his future wife, Justine Karain, often caddying for him. Talk about earning it and keeping it in the family. Justine’s brother, Kessler Karain, has been Reed’s caddie for most of his career, including this year, when he had top-12 finishes in the Masters and the PGA Championship. One of Karain’s responsibilities is to make sure a particular and properly folded American flag is neatly tucked away in Reed’s golf bag, no matter the bag or occasion.

This is the guy who went LIV, signing for millions of guaranteed petrodollars by way of the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund?

Reed announced that he was departing for LIV in June 2022, shortly before the U.S. Open. He announced his departure from LIV, and his return to the PGA Tour, in late January 2026. He didn’t know then that the Saudi funding of the upstart golf league was about to evaporate. He did know that after playing the world for three and a half years, he missed home and his home tour. He missed 72-hole, full-field events with a cut. And he missed the adrenaline rush of PGA Tour golf, playing on a Sunday afternoon with a CBS or NBC camera in your face. He will now be back on the PGA Tour next season, having served his suspension and earned his card via the DP World Tour’s Race to Dubai.

Reed has been playing abroad, and off network TV, for so long now that casual golf fans may be surprised to learn he’s ranked solidly in the top 40 in the world (currently 33rd), and even that shorthand understates how good his golf is. There’s no quit in him, and his swing is a study in arms-to-body connectedness. In other words, it repeats. We’re likely to see a lot of Patrick Reed over the next decade or so, at the four majors, at the Players Championship and other sparkly Tour events and possibly during the most celebrated team events. Could he represent the United States in team events again? For sure.

“When I left the Tour and joined LIV, it was the right thing for me and my family,” Reed said earlier this spring. Actually, he said pretty much the same thing several times, over the course of several interviews. “I really enjoyed my time with LIV. I enjoyed playing all over the world, seeing all these different cultures. But now I’m super excited to be returning to the PGA Tour and ending my career where it began.”

It sounded like a practiced sound bite. It had to be a practiced sound bite. And the statement was surely true, as far as it went. It just didn’t go that far.

The deeper truth is sensitive and complicated and Reed won’t discuss it, at least not publicly, but it explains a great deal.

Reed’s life as a professional golfer is starting to look like a movie in three acts. Everyone who follows golf closely remembers Act I: Reed as a prominent PGA Tour player (nine wins) and repeated on-course rules issues that resulted in criticism on Golf Channel, whispering on Tour and a lot of pointed commentary from golf fans thumbing away, fast and furious, on their favorite social-media platforms. Reed could maybe have handled all that — he has an us-against-the-world mentality. But when his young daughter and son were mocked at school by mean-spirited kids mimicking what they heard at home — Yer dad’s a cheater — Reed decided to take his talents to LIV Golf.

Fewer people saw Act II: Reed as a globetrotting LIV Golf golfer, when, one prominent LIV official told me, Reed was a “perfect gentleman, a pleasure to be with, with no rules issues.” But if Reed took ownership for any of his various rule book episodes, nobody I talked to knew anything about it. Now comes Act III: Reed’s return, possibly with more people watching than ever before.

Reed told me, in a firm and civil tone, that he didn’t want to revisit his past. (I had brought up two rules events, one in 2019 at Tiger’s Hero World Challenge, where Reed was contending; the other at the 2021 Farmers Insurance Open, which Reed won.) I asked him if he had regrets, if there were things he had done for which he’d like a mulligan. No, in a word. “I believe everything happens for a purpose,” Reed said. “Everything in my life, from the time I was born, right through this interview, happens for a reason.” Happens for a reason. He’s not the first person in the history of mankind to cite the phrase.

title: CANADA’S WOMEN’S SEVENS TEAM CONFIRMS ROSTER FOR FIRST TWO STOPS OF 2027 HSBC SVNS SERIES
article_text:
The squad for Canada’s Women’s Sevens Team has been named for the first two tournaments of the 2027 HSBC SVNS Series, with Canada set to play in Dubai on November 28-29 and Cape Town on December 5-6.

November 19, 2026 (Langford, BC) — The squad for Canada’s Women’s Sevens Team has been named for the first two tournaments of the 2027 HSBC SVNS Series, with Canada set to play in Dubai on November 28-29 and Cape Town on December 5-6.

The 2027 HSBC SVNS Series brings an added level of excitement and intrigue, with qualification for the 2028 LA Olympics on the line. The top four teams in the standings following the final tournament in New York, prior to the start of the HSBC SVNS World Championships, will secure Olympic qualification. That number increases to five if the USA finishes among the top four teams.

With Olympic qualification at stake, the 2027 HSBC SVNS Series marks the beginning of Canada’s journey to the LA Olympics in 2028, following the team’s historic performance at the Paris 2024 Olympics, where Canada captured a silver medal.

"The road to LA 2028 is well under way, and our focus is on the opening leg of the 2027 series in Dubai and Cape Town," said Jocelyn Barrieau, Head Coach of Canada's Women's Sevens Team. "This roster reflects both experienced Sevens players that led us to success in the 2025/26 season and some new faces which will continue to build depth across this program in this Olympic qualification season."

Several Canadian players were unavailable for selection as they are competing in the Premiership Women’s Rugby (PWR) league in England. Breanne Nicholas, Adia Pye and Larah Wright are the three returning players from the Canadian squad that captured bronze at the final stop of the 2026 HSBC SVNS World Championship in Bordeaux, France. That tournament marked the last time Canada’s Women’s Sevens Team took the field together.

Set to make their international sevens debuts for Canada are Lizzie Gibson, Aurora Bowie, Ava Van Saten and Olivia Newsome. Gibson and Bowie both featured regularly for Canada’s Women’s 15s Team throughout 2026, while Van Saten was named MVP at the 2026 FISU World University Championships, helping Canada capture gold. Van Saten scored all four of Canada’s tries in a 20-0 victory over France in the final. Newsome recently helped the University of Victoria win gold at the 2026 U SPORTS National Rugby Championship.

Next year, the 2027 HSBC SVNS Series returns to BC Place Stadium in Vancouver on March 6-7. Canadian rugby fans will have the opportunity to watch both Canada’s Men’s and Women’s Sevens Teams compete on home soil. Tickets are available now at vansevens.com.

title: Blitzboks include two uncapped players in Dubai squad as SVNS series returns
article_text:
Blitzbok head coach Philip Snyman has named a 13-man squad for the opening tournament of the season, where Selvyn Davids will also earn his 50th tournament cap.

Former Junior Springbok wing JC Mars has been selected as an outside back, while FNB UP-Tuks centre Van Reenen Kruger has been included among the forwards.

Siviwe Soyizwapi will captain the side in the absence of Impi Visser, having previously led the Blitzboks in Singapore and Perth last season.

Davids is one of six players who featured in last year's Dubai tournament, where South Africa finished fifth. The team bounced back in impressive fashion, winning four tournaments on their way to claiming the overall series title before securing a second successive HSBC SVNS World Championship crown.

The 31-year-old Davids made his international sevens debut in Hong Kong during the 2016/17 season and has since scored 793 points, including 107 tries, for South Africa. Meanwhile, Zain Davids and Ryan Oosthuizen are set to feature in their ninth Dubai tournaments, having each been part of six Blitzbok title-winning campaigns there.

Snyman said selection was based on current form in training, while also taking into account the need to build depth within the squad.

"JC has been in the SA Rugby pathway since his school days, while 'Van' had a brilliant Varsity Cup campaign and once we brought them into the wider group, they quickly rose to the challenge."

Snyman saluted Selvyn Davids, who has also captained the Blitzboks, on his half century: "He is just such an awesome team player and playmaker and to have him fit and ready is just great. The same with Siviwe, who will take the reins with Impi not quite fit and available for this tournament. One of our strengths is a strong leadership group, which makes my life much easier as a coach."

The Dubai tournament takes place on 28 and 29 November and South Africa have been drawn in Pool A with Australia, the USA and Argentina. The series then moves to the DHL Stadium for the HSBC SVNS Cape Town on 5 and 6 December.

Christie Grobbelaar, Ryan Oosthuizen, Zain Davids, Ricardo Duarttee, Quewin Nortje, Selvyn Davids, Dewald Human, Siviwe Soyizwapi (captain), Grant de Jager, Sebastiaan Jobb, JC Mars, Tristan Leyds, Van Reenen Kruger.

title: Hong Kong Open: Evergreen Intanon Books Record Trip
article_text:
Ratchanok Intanon punched her ticket to the season finale for a women’s singles record 11th time after beating Michelle Li 21-19 21-16 in the LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 quarterfinals on Friday.

Needing a victory to secure the ranking points required for next month’s HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 in Hangzhou, the Thai star showed trademark composure to reach her first Hong Kong Open semifinal since finishing runner-up to Chen Yu Fei in 2019.

“I felt like she had some pain or some injury,” Intanon said of Li. “Still, I tried not to think about anything outside the court and just focus on the game. I had to stay calm on every shot because I felt she was slower than me, though her hands were still better than mine on some shots.”

For Intanon, the milestone is a testament to resilience following her own injury battles.

“First of all, I want to thank myself because I never give up through injuries,” she reflected. “Coming back takes time and I’ve tried to take it slowly and manage it with my coach. Even here, I’m still not 100 per cent, so I just wanted to do what I could in the moment.”

Next up is an all-Thai semifinal against compatriot Pornpawee Chochuwong, who defeated Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj by the exact same scoreline moments later. Chochuwong also clinched the final women’s singles berth for Hangzhou after her sole rival, Putri Kusuma Wardani, fell 22-20 22-20 to Wang Zhi Yi.

Despite making 10 prior appearances at the season finale, a title has remained elusive for Intanon.

Her first appearance back in 2012 – at the Super Series Finals – saw her reach the last four, where she lost to Wang Shi Xian.

“I’ve played so many times now. I’m always very grateful and though I’ve never won it, every time I go I hope to at least make that semifinal mark,” she said. “I’m going to take care of my body after this tournament and try to get stronger.”

Asked if she is setting a bigger target this year, her answer was simple: “Winning.”

Amallia Cahaya Pratiwi/Siti Fadia Silva Ramadhanti completed their remarkable rise by claiming a women’spot at the Finals, beating top seeds Yuki Fukushima/Mayu Matsumoto 21-16 21-15.

Languishing in 23rd position just last month, the Indonesians, who only paired up this year, surged into the women’s doubles top eight off the back of a HYLO Open title, deep runs at the French Open and Kumamoto Masters and Friday’s upset. Minutes later, Americans Lauren Lam/Allison Lee’s 21-18 21-11 defeat to Pearly Tan/Thinaah Muralitharan officially sealed Hangzhou berths for both Pratiwi/Ramadhanti and Bulgarian sisters Gabriela Stoeva/Stefani Stoeva.

Pratiwi put their qualification into perspective: “Opportunities truly come from anywhere; we didn’t expect to make it this far.”

Ramadhanti added: “Going through a difficult period and missing out on the Asian Games really served as a wake-up call for us.”

title: BWF World Senior Circuit Hosting Opportunity – 2027
article_text:
Building on the initial circuit tournaments in 2026, and after consultation with key stakeholders, the BWF has confirmed a framework for the BWF World Senior Circuit and welcomes applications from interested Member Associations to host tournaments in 2027.

The establishment of the World Senior Circuit is a key strategic opportunity to engage senior players on a global level to continue to play badminton and to invest in a circuit of sustainable tournaments which culminate in the BWF World Senior Championships as the pinnacle senior badminton tournament.

The following summarises the established framework and application process.

- As a standalone World Senior Circuit tournament or as a joint Continental Confederation Senior Circuit and BWF Senior Circuit tournament.

- The BWF to sanction/confirm World Senior Circuit tournaments.

- Host responsible for delivery of tournament and related costs.

Same as World Senior Championships starting with 35+ up to 75+ with host option to hold more categories (e.g. 80+).

Additional strength categories can be offered (e.g. recreational or a “waterfall” tournament); however, the elite category only counts for the World Senior Ranking.

Player Age Eligibility: Players must fulfil the age requirement before 1 January of the year of the tournament.

- Manual entry process to start (or tournament-specific online entry if applicable).

- Entry fees can be charged to ensure operational sustainability.

- Maximum three events per player (per age group or across varying age groups).

- Group > Knockout if entry size requires (group only if entry size requires) following, where applicable, BWF General Competition Regulations (GCR).

Scoring System: Best of three games to 15 points.

Length of competition up to host based on entry size and other local factors, with last day (finals) on Sunday.

- Prospectus Publication: At least 120 days in advance of tournament.

- Entry deadline: Four weeks in advance of tournament.

- Draws: One week in advance of tournament.

- Based on World Senior Ranking, where applicable, following GCR.

- Substitutions: Allowed for doubles events only, as per BWF World Senior Championships regulations.

- Minimum national level but Continental Level recommended.

- Minimum national level but Continental Level recommended.

- Line Judges: Recruited and provided by host.

Transportation Services: Determined by host, based on entry fees charged.

Accommodation: Determined by host, but at minimum, host to provide list of hotel options for individual player bookings.

Visa Support: Hosting MA to provide visa support letter / other documentation as required.

- Tournament doctor / nurse / paramedics for field of play.

- Medical care for players provided back of house as needed but can be charged to players.

Practice: Where feasible, provide access to competition courts (and practice court(s), if available), but not required.

A set of formalised regulations will be confirmed and published based on the above framework in due course.

The BWF is accepting applications from Member Associations to host World Senior Circuit tournaments in 2027 (with the option to confirm continued hosting in 2028) through submission of a Sanction Request by 31 December 2026 via the following form.

Please note that for 2027 tournaments, the earliest hosting opportunity would be March 2027.

The BWF to confirm hosts by January 2027 and establish a calendar of tournaments.

The BWF to provide further guidance to hosting Member Associations in January or February 2027.

title: Verizon renews LaLiga sponsorship amid World Cup years
article_text:
Seven years after first signing on as a regional sponsor of LaLiga in the US and Canada, Verizon is renewing the deal under another multiyear agreement, the Spanish pro soccer league shared exclusively with Marketing Brew.

It’s the second time Verizon has re-upped its LaLiga sponsorship that began in the 2019-20 season, after first renewing it in 2023. The announcement comes sandwiched between two World Cups, with the men’s tournament held this past summer in North America, and the women’s coming up in Brazil next year.

With soccer fandom making strides in the US following the World Cup, Verizon has looked to stake its claim in the sport in a way that could help the brand stand out among other sponsors. In addition to serving as the official wireless telecommunications partner of LaLiga in the US and Canada, Verizon is hosting sweepstakes that provide fans access to the league, a sponsorship strategy the brand has carried over from its NFL and World Cup work.

For LaLiga, brands that want to activate experientially as opposed to just through official marks or media buys can help support the mission of growing fandom around the world, Nicolás García Hemme, managing director of LaLiga North America, told Marketing Brew.

“We go to market together, and the fans feel that the brand is very much there with LaLiga,” Hemme said. “It’s not just LaLiga delivering a logo.”

The latest deal focuses on the brand’s Verizon Shine loyalty program, which offers sweepstakes and merch drops through its app that include experiences with LaLiga like trips to Spain and meet and greets with legends from the league.

“Extending our long-standing partnership with LaLiga allows us to meaningfully fuel soccer fandom as momentum continues to surge,” Justin Toman, Verizon’s VP of partnerships, said in an email.

One complication to growing fandom is that soccer is a fragmented sport, Hemme said, and not just in terms of media rights.

“When you talk about basketball, you have the NBA,” he said. “When you talk about American football, you have the NFL. Then you talk soccer, and you have local soccer with MLS and the NWSL, then you have Liga MX, a huge deal here in the US due to the Hispanic population, and you have all the European soccer competition coming to the market.”

To stand out to sponsors in the US—which also include Walmart and Lowe’s—Hemme said his team leans into a few selling points of LaLiga, including some of its teams with rabid global fandom like Real Madrid and FC Barcelona, as well as the league’s connection with various Hispanic communities.

LaLiga’s growing audience in the US certainly doesn’t hurt among brands, either. The league had record US viewership across ESPN platforms for its 2025-26 season with more than 20 million viewers, up 10% YoY.

After the World Cup, Barcelona and Elche CF opened the 2026-27 season with 1 million viewers on ESPN platforms, making it the most-watched English-language match for LaLiga on the network. El Clásico, the iconic matchup between Barcelona and Real Madrid, averaged 2.4 million viewers on ABC and ESPN Deportes last month, up more than 50% from last season to become the most-watched LaLiga match for ESPN.

The involvement of sponsors like Verizon help support LaLiga’s efforts to grow that fandom even further, especially as the league looks to build its reputation among people outside of its core audience of Hispanic fans, Hemme said.

“For these [new] audiences,” he said, “you have to find other angles” to build affinity, including the more lifestyle-oriented experiences.

title: Leicester City terminate shirt sponsorship after adult film star backlash
article_text:
There was a time when Leicester City could do no wrong.

The Foxes went from one of the greatest underdog stories in sporting history to FA Cup winners, capturing the imagination of football supporters around the world. Today, however, the club find themselves fighting a very different battle, with financial troubles, successive relegations and a series of controversies threatening to tarnish their remarkable legacy.

Their latest scandal, involving a betting sponsor and an adult film performer, is perhaps another indication of just how difficult it has been for the club to find stability.

Few will ever forget their remarkable and awe-inspiring English Premier League championship run that had the entire world rooting for them during the 2015/16 season. As recently as 2021, the Foxes lifted the FA Cup.

Since those heady days, though, the club has been mired in controversy and a fall from grace that will be noted in the history books for years to come, with that cup triumph one of the few bright spots.

In 2025, the club was relegated from the elite division to the Championship, and a year later they dropped down again to League One. Currently, they are 11th in the third tier, having won only five of their 14 matches thus far.

Financial mismanagement, a carousel of managers and breaches of league financial rules have plagued the club since their famous title-winning campaign. But their latest controversy has further undermined their standing.

As reported by several media outlets, including the BBC, Leicester's main shirt sponsor, BC.GAME, parted ways with the club this week following a backlash over the betting company's appointment of Russian adult film performer Eva Elfie as their brand ambassador. Setting aside Elfie's appointment, with the company justifying her appointment due to her reach within the eSports and gaming communities, the BC.GAME sponsorship had been heavily questioned since its announcement in 2024, given that the company is an unlicensed gambling company in the UK.

In response to the Elfie announcement, the Foxes Trust — who are the official supporters' club of the team — said in a statement this week: "Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people.

"Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?"

In response, the club issued a statement on Wednesday confirming that the sponsorship had been terminated by "mutual consent" with immediate effect. They also announced a returns policy for supporters who had bought shirts bearing the BC.GAME branding through official club channels within the previous 28 days.

"Since the partnership was announced in 2024, the trust has consistently made clear that BC Game, for numerous reasons, does not reflect the values of our club or its supporters," the Foxes Trust said, after the sponsorship was terminated.

"That view has been shared by the great majority of fans who responded to our surveys. The recent partnership with an adult content creator only deepened those concerns and the trust felt the need to once again speak out publicly.

"This statement gained strong traction, emphasising the weight of feeling on this matter. Although we believe that the club should never have gone into partnership with BC Game, we nevertheless welcome this decision to part ways."

title: Formula 1 Signs with Nike Across F1 and F1 ACADEMY
article_text:
Formula 1 has entered a long-term global partnership with Nike, uniting motorsport’s premier championship with the world’s largest athletic footwear and apparel brand across both Formula 1 and F1 ACADEMY.

Ahead of the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, the agreement establishes Nike as an Official Partner and the Official Apparel and Uniform Supplier of Formula 1 beginning in the 2027 season, while also naming Nike an Official Partner and Official Sporting Apparel Partner of F1 ACADEMY.

Formula 1 president and CEO, Stefano Domenicali, emphasised the cultural reach and global momentum driving the alliance across both series.

“Formula 1 and Nike are two of the world’s most iconic brands, united by a relentless drive to innovate, perform at the highest level, and inspire people to push beyond what is possible.”

“Formula 1 is experiencing unprecedented global growth, reaching hundreds of millions of fans and engaging one of the most passionate, diverse and dynamic communities in sport.

“Nike’s unique ability to sit at the intersection of sport, culture and inspiration makes them the ideal partner as we enter our next chapter,” Domenicali said.

Nike president and CEO, Elliott Hill, highlighted the shared performance ethos connecting motorsport with Nike’s global athlete mandate.

“Formula 1 is driven by competition, speed and a constant push to innovate.”

“That’s an athlete mindset, and it’s one we share at Nike.

“Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes and inspire fans around the world,” Hill said.

From 2027, Nike will supply co-branded uniforms for Formula 1 staff at events worldwide while rolling out performance innovations, footwear, apparel, accessories, and race-weekend fan experiences across the global calendar. Ahead of the full commercial rollout, an early preview arrives on 20 November 2026 with a limited-edition Las Vegas Grand Prix x Nike capsule collection launching at the F1 Hub and Nike retail locations in Las Vegas.

title: Equiti reveals official sports event partnership with Rolex SailGP 2026
article_text:
Equiti Group, a global fintech, has partnered with the 2026 Rolex SailGP Championship. The event partnership unites the two brands, Equiti and SailGP, around a shared belief that ambitious ideas, new technology and world-class experiences should reach more people.

Equiti will bring its brand to life across SailGP’s global platform, starting with the Emirates Dubai Sail Grand Prix, presented by DP World, on 21–22 November and at the season’s grande finale: the Mubadala Abu Dhabi Sail Grand Prix, presented by Abu Dhabi Sports Council, on 28–29 November.

Across both race weekends, Equiti will bring the partnership to life through bespoke brand and digital activations.

Equiti joins a strong SailGP partner line-up that includes Rolex, DP World, Emirates, Mubadala, Oracle, Apex Group, Accor, KPMG and Red Bull.

Founded by Larry Ellison and Sir Russell Coutts, and title-sponsored by Rolex, the championship combines elite athleticism, cutting-edge technology and real-time data to deliver fast, close racing. National teams race identical F50 hydrofoiling catamarans, at speeds sometimes exceeding 100kmph.

The SailGP 2025 Season reached a cumulative global broadcast audience of nearly 215 million viewers, averaging 18 million viewers per event, while SailGP content generated more than 1.65 billion social media views. More than 112,000 fans attended events across the season, underscoring the league’s growing appeal both in venues and on screen.

Chantelle Johnson, Chief Marketing Officer, Equiti Group, said, “SailGP is one of the fastest-growing sports in the world. Not just because it brings ambitious people together, but because it refuses to settle for what has been done before. Equiti is proud to join that shared platform. We both believe in challenging the status quo, raising the bar and creating experiences that bring more people into the action.”

SailGP is built around innovative technology and a refusal to accept limits, bringing world-class racing to a broad audience while its teams, owners and investors keep redefining what is possible on the water. Equiti shares that drive, using technology to open up access without diluting quality, and help people build better money habits.

Charlie Dewhurst, Chief Commercial Officer, SailGP, said, “We’re very pleased to partner with Equiti on two of our biggest races of the season in the UAE, in Dubai and our Grand Final in Abu Dhabi.

Dewhurst added, “We share their commitment to innovation and have a real alignment in our approach to data and precision across both our worlds of trading and sail racing. They are committed to elevating the fan experience across both events and we look forward to evolving this partnership in what is a very important region for SailGP.”

title: USA confirm Ilona Maher's return for start of new SVNS campaign
article_text:
Ilona Maher will make her return to HSBC SVNS Series action in Dubai and Cape Town at the start of the 2026/27 season.

The 30-year-old did not play for the USA Women’s Eagles Sevens last season after her involvement at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025. She is the third-most experienced player named in Emilie Bydwell’s squad for the first tournaments of the new campaign.

Emilie Bydwell, USA Women’s Eagles Sevens head coach, said: “Beyond who she is as a player, she’s such a professional. She takes what she does here very seriously, and she’s such a competitor.

“It’s been really great to have her back in – ready to compete, ready to drive the standards that we have as a team, and ready to empower the young athletes that she’s playing alongside.”

Maher’s return adds to an otherwise settled squad, with travelling reserve Fane Tausinga the only player named without any tournament caps.

Last season, the Eagles finished fourth after three HSBC SVNS World Championship tournaments. While other teams are looking to book their place at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles, as host nation the Eagles can focus on development hot on the heels of a positive campaign.

Bydwell said: “We want a storm-proof performance this year. We want to be really consistent, regardless of what lineup we put on the field, who we’re playing, or what game we’re playing in.

“We’ve come back into these two weeks of training hitting the ground running. We still have stuff that we need to clean up and can still be better. Our preseason was a long eight weeks before we were in New Zealand, and no matter how well it’s planned, it’s just not the same as playing.”

For Dubai, the USA have been named in Pool A alongside Spain, France and Australia.

title: Springboks demand World Rugby action as Ireland accusation made on eve of game
article_text:
Mzwandile Stick, South Africa's assistant coach, has demanded clarity from World Rugby over the new hip-drop tackle law, claiming Ireland's Sam Prendergast would have been banned for the tackle he was cited for last weekend were he a Fijian.

The Irish fly-half was summoned over an alleged hip-drop tackle on Fiji captain Peceli Yato last weekend but escaped punishment, being cleared of the charge after he contested it earlier this week.

He is now free to face the Springboks this weekend, something which South Africa have taken umbrage with.

Their head coach, Rassie Erasmus, is already serving a six-match ban for comments he made in the aftermath of South Africa's defeat to France last weekend, where he questioned whether referees were involved in "match-fixing" and accused officials of missing 17 on-field infringements in Paris, among other things.

Now Stick has issued a defiant statement to World Rugby, saying the squad is united and that Erasmus' suspension won't split the camp.

“Rassie might not be in that coaching box, but he’s with us,” he said. “His energy will be there. And whatever we’re going to be doing tomorrow, we’ll do it for him. No one is going to break us.”

Moving on to Prendergast, Stick suggested the No.10 should have been banned and would have been, had he been a Fiji player.

“You know what they call a traditional drink in Fiji?" he said.

"Is it kava? If that was a Fijian player, he would be sitting in Fiji now doing some extra lessons of how to tackle. But it’s an Irish player, it’s free to play."

He added they as coaches needed clarity from law makers in order to instruct their players, who he claims are in the dark right now.

“When there are laws and new rules, people need to explain,” he said. “The players look up to us as coaches. They also don’t know what’s right or wrong.”

He added: “We want to play the game clean and make sure players know how to tackle. But other parties aren’t coming to the party, and then we’re getting punished.”

Stick implied that suspensions were becoming "a trend" when visiting the Emerald Isle, with Jasper Wiese hit with a ban following his red card against Les Bleus and therefore unavailable for the match tomorrow.

“Last year in this boardroom, we were talking about [players] who were also suspended. It’s becoming a trend now when you come to Ireland,” he said.

“It’s always crazy now. If I think about last year in this boardroom, we were talking about who was also suspended.

“So it’s becoming a trend now when you come to Ireland, players will be suspended. So I think by the time we come here, we must always be prepared for that.

“But once again, don’t worry, it’s part of the game. I know I’m excited to see a guy like (Cameron) Hanekom also getting an opportunity (in place of Wiese).”

title: Ireland prop stood down with immediate effect ahead of Springboks match
article_text:
Ireland have been dealt a late injury blow ahead of tomorrow’s Nations Championship showdown against South Africa, with Sam Illo ruled out of the clash.

The Connacht prop had initially been named in Andy Farrell’s matchday 23, taking the number 18 shirt, but has now been withdrawn after failing to complete the return-to-play protocols.

Illo suffered a concussion during the second half of last weekend’s victory over Fiji at the Aviva Stadium and has not recovered in time to face the world champions.

Leinster prop Thomas Clarkson has been drafted into the squad as his replacement, while Connacht’s Finlay Bealham has also joined the Ireland camp as emergency cover.

Clarkson is in line to make his first appearance of the month and could find himself facing either Gerhard Steenekamp or Ox Nche in the South African front row, depending on the Springboks' substitutions.

Illo’s absence is a setback for Ireland, particularly given the strength of the Springboks scrum. The late change also means Farrell will have to adjust his front-row options just a day before kick-off.

However, Clarkson is no stranger to the international set-up. The Leinster tighthead was selected as injury cover for the 2025 British and Irish Lions tour of Australia and is listed at 3kg heavier than Illo.

Saturday’s encounter is effectively a must-win for both sides as they look to finish top of their respective hemisphere tables and secure the best possible position heading into next weekend’s finals at Allianz Stadium.

Both Ireland and South Africa currently sit one point behind the leaders in their respective tables.

The Springboks will know exactly what is required when they take to the pitch, with New Zealand facing England earlier in the day.

Ireland, meanwhile, will have to wait until France’s later meeting with Argentina to discover the full picture in their race for top spot.

title: Wales v Australia moved off ITV1 as Nations Championship TV schedule changes
article_text:
Wales' Nations Championship clash with Australia will not be shown on ITV1 this weekend, with a packed international rugby schedule and a busy Saturday night television line-up seeing the match broadcast on ITV4 instead.

Steve Tandy's side host the Wallabies at the Principality Stadium on Saturday, November 21, with kick-off scheduled for the unusually late time of 8.10pm.

However, supporters thinking the match will be on ITV1 will need to switch channels, with the broadcaster instead showing The 1% Club and I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here!

It is a different arrangement for the final round of Nations Championship fixtures, with all six matches taking place on Saturday and three pairs of games kicking off simultaneously.

England's clash with New Zealand, fresh from their defeat in Cardiff last weekend, at Twickenham will be shown on ITV1 at 2.10pm, while Scotland's meeting with Japan takes place at the same time on ITV4.

Ireland then face world champions South Africa at 4.40pm on ITV1, with Italy hosting Fiji simultaneously on ITV4.

The evening sees Wales take on Australia at 8.10pm, at exactly the same time as France host Argentina in Paris. The latter fixture has been allocated ITV2, leaving Wales' encounter with the Wallabies on ITV4.

ITV1's evening schedule includes Celebrity Catchphrase at 7.15pm, The 1% Club at 8.10pm and I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! at 9.15pm.

The scheduling means ITV1 will broadcast two Nations Championship matches during the afternoon before switching away from live rugby for its primetime entertainment programmes.

Despite the change, Wales supporters will still be able to watch the match free-to-air, with ITV4 and ITVX providing English-language coverage.

Welsh-language coverage will also be available on S4C, with streaming available on S4C Clic and BBC iPlayer.

The weekend marks the final round of the inaugural Nations Championship before the competition's finals weekend at Twickenham from November 27 to 29.

- 2.10pm: England v New Zealand – ITV1, ITVX

- 4.40pm: Ireland v South Africa – ITV1, ITVX

- 8.10pm: France v Argentina – ITV2, ITVX

- 8.10pm: Wales v Australia – ITV4, ITVX, S4C, BBC iPlayer

title: Five things Rassie Erasmus is banned from doing against Ireland
article_text:
Springboks boss Rassie Erasmus will be forced to watch Saturday's blockbuster clash against Ireland from afar as he begins his six-match suspension.

The South Africa head coach was hit with the lengthy ban following his controversial comments about the officiating during last Friday's defeat to France.

Ireland legend Brian O’Driscoll has admitted Erasmus has a point, while Eddie Jones has also delivered his verdict on the suspension. SA Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing following the suspension.

However, Erasmus has found a unique way to remain involved by announcing his own live watchalong.

Here, RUCK looks at five things the Springboks boss is banned from doing.

Erasmus cannot even enter the Aviva Stadium as a spectator.

That rules out watching from the stands, a hospitality box or his usual position alongside the coaching team.

Instead, the 54-year-old will watch the fixture from his hotel.

The Springboks boss is prohibited from coaching on matchday.

That means no motivational pre-match speeches, half-time team talks or tactical instructions in the changing room.

Captain Siya Kolisi, who has publicly backed Erasmus following his ban, will have an even greater leadership role.

Perhaps the most significant restriction is the ban on communicating with players and team management on matchday.

Erasmus cannot recommend substitutions, send tactical instructions or use a third party to pass on messages.

Ironically, Christophe Ridley, who was involved in last weekend's controversial defeat to France, will referee Saturday's showdown.

Erasmus cannot contact the match officials on matchday or take part in the formal referee feedback process.

The two-time Rugby World Cup-winning coach is also barred from carrying out media duties during his suspension.

That means no official pre-match interviews or post-match press conferences.

Could Rassie Erasmus land himself in more trouble?

According to Sky Sports, Erasmus could risk breaching his suspension if members of the Springboks coaching staff tune into his planned live stream and receive tactical guidance.

The South African has stressed that the watchalong is a personal event rather than an official Springboks broadcast.

title: Leon Smith: Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain stepping down after 17 years
article_text:
Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain Leon Smith says it is the "right time" for a change after announcing he will end his 17-year stint in the role.

Smith guided the British men's team to Davis Cup victory in 2015 - the nation's first win in the event since 1936.

The 50-year-old Scot said he had been mulling over his future for "most of this year" before deciding to step down after next week's Finals in Bologna.

Smith's successor has not yet been appointed, but the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) has spoken to potential candidates and hopes to announce the new captain as soon as possible.

Former world number one Andy Murray, who was instrumental in Britain's 2015 triumph, is not believed to be interested in the role at this time.

"There comes a time whether it is personally you need a change, or it is good for the team to have something else," said Smith, who seemed emotional in a video call with reporters.

"I've done it for a very long time and I think there are others who will enjoy the role and can bring something different to the role."

"I love the role and haven't lost any passion for it. But it feels like the right time for me personally and the guys moving forwards."

With Smith picking the team and creating a tight bond between the group, Murray was the driving force on the court as he won all eight of his singles matches in the victorious campaign.

Murray was coached by Smith as a child and said winning the Davis Cup together was "one of the proudest moments" of his career.

"He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play. He got the best out of us that year," three-time Grand Slam champion Murray said.

"I've obviously known Leon a long time, I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup and Leon was on the bench. I'm really glad we got to share those moments.

"I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain."

Smith, who will continue in his role as head of British men's tennis, took over in 2010 with the team in danger of being relegated to the lowest tier of the Davis Cup.

Within three years they were back in the top tier and just two years later Murray inspired them to the trophy.

Smith also guided the team to the semi-finals in 2016 and 2019.

While he can no longer rely on a superstar of Murray's ilk, Smith is hoping this year's crop can ensure his captaincy ends on another high.

Britain will rely on Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery and former world number eight Cameron Norrie in the singles, with world number one Henry Patten and three-time major champion Neal Skupski pairing up in the doubles.

Smith's side faces Germany - led by singles world number one Alexander Zverev - in the last eight on Thursday.

"I'm focused and really looking forward to captaining Great Britain for one more week in Bologna next week and hopefully creating a few more special memories together," Smith added.

Smith has won 70% of his ties since taking over as captain in the summer of 2010.

The venues and the crowds for many of the early ties were on the low side, until Britain moved through the divisions and Andy Murray returned to the team.

The travelling support surged, and the team celebrated their return to the World Group with a stunning win over the United States in a baseball stadium in San Diego in January 2014.

Less than two years later the Davis Cup was back in Britain as thrilling wins in Glasgow and the Queen's Club were followed by Murray's famous lob to seal victory over Belgium.

Great attention to detail has contributed to Britain's success; and far more often than not, Smith got the marginal selection calls right.

He will be an extremely hard act to follow, but will inevitably work closely with his successor given his ongoing role as the head of men's tennis.

title: How sustainability is shaping the Nitto ATP Finals
article_text:
The Nitto ATP Finals is about more than just the on-court action.

As well as bringing together the world's best players for the prestigious year-end tournament, the event provides an opportunity to make a positive impact beyond tennis, with sustainability and community engagement central to its wider ambitions.

At the 2026 edition in Turin, title partner Nitto is continuing its work with the ATP, the Italian Tennis and Padel Federation (FITP) and the City of Turin through the Torino Green Project, while introducing new measures to reduce the tournament's environmental footprint.

For this year's event, a hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) fuel blend is being used in the on-site generators in place of conventional diesel. The generators accounted for 36 per cent of the tournament's emissions in 2025, making this an important step towards the event's goal of reducing carbon emissions by 30 per cent by 2030, compared with 2024 levels. Nitto is supporting that ambition through a five-year commitment.

The initiative builds on the Torino Green Project, launched in 2023 by Nitto, FITP, the City of Turin and the ATP. Its first projects included planting 50 trees near the arena, installing green roofs on selected bus stops and donating €100,000 to the city.

The project has continued to evolve. In 2024, a living Green Wall was installed in the Fan Village and later relocated elsewhere in Turin. In 2025, a Green Art Wall, created using air-purifying Airlite paint, was installed at Leone Sinigaglia primary school.

Other measures supporting the tournament's sustainability efforts include electricity from 100 per cent renewable sources, an electrified Lexus fleet for player and staff transport, discounted Frecciarossa train tickets for fans and free travel on selected tram lines for ticket holders.

Sustainability is also reflected in the tournament's community work. Children and families supported by Turin charity U.G.I. ODV are invited to attend matches, while children have the opportunity to walk on court alongside players as mascots. The Nitto ATP Finals Innovation Summit also brings together representatives from the City of Turin, academia and industry to discuss sustainability challenges.

The tournament's environmental progress is measured by FITP, with support from Enovation Consulting, through carbon-footprint assessments and an annual ESG report. The 2025 edition was also certified to the ISO 20121:2024 sustainable event management standard by Bureau Veritas.

With Nitto's title partnership running through 2030, the host city will continue working with its partners and the to make progress towards its emissions-reduction goal.

title: Zi Yu-Noraqilah reach first Super 500 semi-final in World Tour
article_text:
KUALA LUMPUR: Women's pair Low Zi Yu-Noraqilah Maisarah Ramdan celebrated a major milestone after reaching their first Super 500 semi-final at the Hong Kong Open on Friday.

The world No. 41 upset American world No. 25 Francesca Corbett-Jennie Gai 21-19, 16-21, 21-16 in the quarter-finals at the Kai Tak Arena.

The victory came a day after Zi Yu-Noraqilah upset Taiwan's world No. 6 Hsu Yin Hui-Lin Jhih Yun 21-19, 21-18 in the second round.

"I'm very happy because this is our first Super 500 semi-final," said Zi Yu.

Noraqilah felt the pair had produced their best performance of the week against the Americans.

"I think today we played quite well compared with the two previous matches," she said.

Their creditable run has come despite Noraqilah still working her way back to full fitness following a left ankle injury.

The 19-year-old, who withdrew from last week's Kumamoto Masters, said she was currently at 70 per cent fitness.

Noraqilah said preparation for the Hong Kong Open had been demanding, with Zi Yu returning from junior tournament commitments while she was recovering from injury.

They will face either seniors Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah or another American pair, Lauren Lam-Allison Lee, for a place in the final.

title: Wang Zhiyi and Tomoka Miyazaki vie for Hong Kong Open title without Ahn
article_text:
A showdown between the top players from China and Japan will decide who takes the crown at the Hong Kong Open, with badminton world No. 1 Ahn Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) absent.

World No. 3 Wang Zhiyi and No. 7 Tomoka Miyazaki will meet in the Hong Kong Open semifinals. Both are set for a must-win battle as they pursue a place in the final and the title.

Wang Zhiyi and Miyazaki both won their women's singles quarterfinals on the 20th at the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Hong Kong Open (Super 500) at Kai Tak Arena in Hong Kong, securing places in the semifinals.

Wang Zhiyi was first to reach the semifinals after a hard-fought match. She beat Indonesia's Putri Kusuma Wardani, ranked No. 9 in the world, 2-0 (22-20, 22-20). Both games went to deuce at 20-20, but Wang stayed focused at the decisive moments and closed out the match with consecutive points.

The win was also significant because Wang was the last Chinese woman left in the singles draw. Tokyo Olympic gold medalist Chen Yufei, ranked No. 4 in the world, lost to India's Santoshi Ramraj, while Han Yue and Su Wenjing were also eliminated. Wang was the only Chinese player left, preserving her country's pride.

Miyazaki also secured a semifinal berth with a dominant performance. She routed fellow Japanese player Hina Akechi, ranked No. 14 in the world, 2-0 (21-11, 21-9). After coming back from an early deficit in the first game, she extended her lead with a run of points. She then put Akechi under pressure from the start of the second game and won comfortably.

The victory also served as revenge for Miyazaki. She put behind her a painful 2-1 comeback loss to Akechi in the Korea Open quarterfinals on the 6th in Yeosu, South Jeolla province.

The two players will now face off for a place in the final. Wang remains China's only hope in women's singles, while Miyazaki has an opportunity to prove herself as the next ace of Japanese women's badminton.

The title race has become more competitive with world No. 1 Ahn Se-young (Samsung Life Insurance), No. 2 Akane Yamaguchi of Japan and No. 5 Pusarla Venkata Sindhu of India all absent from the tournament. With the dominant favorite out, Wang and Miyazaki have emerged as title contenders.

Wang has shown her determination to reclaim the title, surviving to the semifinals as the only Chinese player left in the tournament. Miyazaki has already secured a spot in the 2026 BWF World Tour Finals and is determined to keep her momentum going with a title win ahead of the season-ending event.

If both players win their semifinals, they will advance to the final, where they will be just one match away from the title. With Ahn absent from the Hong Kong Open, attention is focused on whether China's Wang will challenge for the title or Japan's Miyazaki will emerge as the new queen.
